shortDescription: For every year that a girl is enrolled in school, she is more likely to avoid early marriage and to survive childbirth. She will be less likely to suffer domestic violence, or be trafficked, and will have a higher future income. She will have a smaller, healthier family and will be 50% more likely to immunize her kids. She’ll leave her mark on future generations, as climate scientists rank girls’ education as number six out of 80 actions that can reverse global warming. And she’ll be twice as likely to educate her own girls — keeping the cycle going. Yet despite all these proven economic and societal benefits, across the globe, millions of girls are still excluded from school because of their gender. India is home to one of the largest such populations, with more than 4.1 million girls outside the classroom. Educate Girls are supporting 1.6 million girls in rural India to gain access to education, and you can help them by mapping and validating villages in rural India.

shortDescription: For every year that a girl is enrolled in school, she is more likely to avoid early marriage and to survive childbirth. She will be less likely to suffer domestic violence, or be trafficked, and will have a higher future income. She will have a smaller, healthier family and will be 50% more likely to immunize her kids. She’ll leave her mark on future generations, as climate scientists rank girls’ education as number six out of 80 actions that can reverse global warming. And she’ll be twice as likely to educate her own girls — keeping the cycle going. Yet despite all these proven economic and societal benefits, across the globe, millions of girls are still excluded from school because of their gender. India is home to one of the largest such populations, with more than 4.1 million girls outside the classroom. Educate Girls are supporting 1.6 million girls in rural India to gain access to education, and you can help them by mapping and validating villages in rural India.

name: Karwi 1, Chitrakoot district
shortDescription: For every year that a girl is enrolled in school, she is more likely to avoid early marriage and to survive childbirth. She will be less likely to suffer domestic violence, or be trafficked, and will have a higher future income. She will have a smaller, healthier family and will be 50% more likely to immunize her kids. She’ll leave her mark on future generations, as climate scientists rank girls’ education as number six out of 80 actions that can reverse global warming. And she’ll be twice as likely to educate her own girls — keeping the cycle going. Yet despite all these proven economic and societal benefits, across the globe, millions of girls are still excluded from school because of their gender. India is home to one of the largest such populations, with more than 4.1 million girls outside the classroom. Educate Girls are supporting 1.6 million girls in rural India to gain access to education, and you can help them by mapping and validating villages in rural India.

She will be less likely to suffer domestic violence, or be trafficked, and will have a higher future income. She will have a smaller, healthier family and will be 50% more likely to immunize her kids. She’ll leave her mark on future generations, as climate scientists rank girls’ education as number six out of 80 actions that can reverse global warming. And she’ll be twice as likely to educate her own girls — keeping the cycle going. Yet despite all these proven economic and societal benefits, across the globe, millions of girls are still excluded from school because of their gender. India is home to one of the largest such populations, with more than 4.1 million girls outside the classroom. Educate Girls are supporting 1.6 million girls in rural India to gain access to education, and you can help them by mapping and validating villages in rural India.

name: Missing Maps: Beboro, Moissala, Chad - update
shortDescription:
MSF has a maternal and child health support program in the health district of Moissala in Chad. With help of a first remote mapping of the area MSF was able to get a better population estimation. However the data needs now an update on the latest available imagery.

The mapping will help MSF to have an overview of all households (represented by roofs) and draw a sample of the population. The data will help in better programming health activities.

**The area was largely mapped using outdated Bing imagery. Since the area has evolved in the meantime, we need an update of the data in the area with more recent imagery. Please do delete mapped buildings if it does no longer corresponds to the new reality that you can see on the Maxar Premium Imagery.**

name: Local Trails and Community Infrastructure Mapping for Emergency Preparedness and Response of Bajhang district of Nepal
shortDescription:
“Local Trails and Infrastructure Mapping for Emergency Preparedness and Response” is a data collection and mapping initiative aimed at fulfilling the data gaps in some of the remotest and most vulnerable locations in Nepal. The initiative is being implemented by the [WFP NEPAL](https://www.wfp.org/countries/nepal) and different local companies with expertise in GIS Mapping and OSM. [NAXA](https://naxa.com.np), a location based service provider company will be working as a technical partner in the project. Besides remote mapping and OSM, the locals from project areas will be trained and mobilized for almost a month to collect all datasets on ground. All the datasets through remote mapping and field based data collection will be used to create maps and geo databases of local units and will also be submitted to the local governments.

This TM project is coordinated by [NAXA](https://naxa.com.np) in partnership with [Youthmappers](https://youthmappers.org) and [GES](http://ges.ku.edu.np) supported by Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs & Trade, [DFAT](https://www.dfat.gov.au/) and implemented by [WFP Nepal](https://www.wfp.org/countries/nepal).

name: Trail and Community Infrastructure Mapping for Emergency Preparedness and Response in Kalikot District
shortDescription: ‘Trail and Community Infrastructure Mapping’ is an initiative of the World Food Programme (WFP) to address spatial data gap of the remotest and most vulnerable communities of Nepal and to prepare local communities for emergency preparedness and response. In this initiative, the locals from project areas will be sensitized, trained and mobilized for mapping 500KM of major supply routes (main trial), community assets, critical access infrastructure, hazard location and other access constraints along the trail routes. Furthermore, remote mapping will be conducted to map the elements at risk such as building footprints, road/trail networks, bridges and waterways engaging digital volunteers. The data collected from remote and field mapping will be validated. A Geo-database along with Geo-tagged images, printed maps and reports at will be handed over to local government.

shortDescription: ‘Trail and Community Infrastructure Mapping’ is an initiative of the World Food Programme (WFP) to address spatial data gap of the remotest and most vulnerable communities of Nepal and to prepare local communities for emergency preparedness and response. In this initiative the locals from project areas will be sensitized, trained and mobilized for mapping 500KM of major supply routes (main trial), community assets, critical access infrastructure, hazard location and other access constraints along the trail routes. Furthermore, remote mapping will be conducted to map the elements at risk such as building footprints, road/trail networks, bridges and waterways engaging digital volunteers. The data collected from remote and field mapping will be validated. A Geo-database along with Geo-tagged images, printed maps and reports at will be handed over to local government.

shortDescription:

name: Daboya (R109), Ghana #Leclara, #liei-larabanga
shortDescription:
You are kindly asked to familiarize yourself with the following instructions before you begin.
>==> When working with __JOSM__ (recommended!) please remember to use __ONLY__ the __project _default_ imagery__. (_These may be greyscale (black and white) or coloured_). 

>==> For __ID-Editor__, please  choose __Custom__ imagery (when available). _Otherwise_ use __Maxar Premium__ but only if it __not__ identical to the Bing imagery!
==> __DO NOT use Bing__ or any other sources as they are _completely outdated_.


There are some round huts, mostly in rural areas. Otherwise, do not forget to square building corners (not a problem if you use JOSM's "Buildings Tool" to map.) You will only occasionally find buildings which do not have right-angle corners.
Note that there may be numerous buildings in towns (or otherwise) requiring a relation of `type=multipolygon` (with roles "outer","inner").

As necessary, use `building=construction`. (These appear as grid-like patterns on the ground.)

The major paved (national) highways in the area (N7,N12 and/or N10) are already mapped.
Otherwise, map clearly visible roads, tracks and paths connecting towns and settlements. Other major highways between towns can be marked `highway=unclassified` but _most_ should be labelled as either `highway=track` if it looks like traffic can pass, otherwise `highway=path`. 

__Do__ __NOT__ __map__ the many tracks or paths which end in farming fields (or "the middle of nowhere").

shortDescription:
Since 2017, CartONG and its community of volunteers have been involved in the mapping of several refugee camps that do not yet appear on any map. 

Currently the organizations in charge of these camps that ensure access to basic facilities and provide humanitarian aid don't have up-to-date maps on the areas in question. Once the map is completed remotely on OpenStreetMap, the operators in the field will add additional data on the infrastructures. The maps then created will be used for refugee camp planning  in order to improve the living conditions of the communities.

name: Missing Maps: Niger, Goure (East)
shortDescription: The Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre, Niger Red Cross Society and the French Red Cross, with funding from AFD and Cooperation Monegasque are implementing a project - to build the resilience of agro-pastoral communities in the Zinder region, Niger against food insecurity and nutrition crisis from Drought. Funding from the British Red Cross will support to expand the project. The data contributed will be used to assist in forecasting future disaster impacts, by knowing in advance where is likely to be impacted and its exposure and vulnerability. The information will help implementation of early action activities in response to a forecasted drought, before it occurs, contributing to reduce risk, prepare for effective response and ultimately to strengthen community resilience.

name: SSSI | FireWaterMapathon | Great Ocean Road
shortDescription:
In response to the national bushfires which devastated many parts of Australia in late 2019 – 2020, the Surveying & Spatial Science Institute marshalled a significant surveying and spatial volunteer network to collect data on burnt infrastructure. The SSSI National Bushfire Recovery Map-a-thon was held in early February, 2020, with over 600 volunteers participating from over 25 different countries.   

The Map-a-thon was one of the largest single event map-a-thons held in the Australasian region; with a total of 2,793,879 hectares were mapped, with 15,731 edits, 13,891 building edits, 1,091 damaged features mapped and 945 damaged buildings mapped. The data collected was used as a guide for recovery efforts to supplement authoritative data sources where no data exists.

The previous Map-a-thon focused on bushfire recovery; this Map-a-thon focuses on bushfire preparedness. During bushfires, firefighters often have difficulty sourcing water. In some regional locations mains water may not be accessible to fight a major bushfire. Static water supplies, such as swimming pools, tanks and dams, are vital sources of water for firefighters. This map-a-thon seeks to map swimming pools, tanks and dams to update Australia’s Static Water Supply System.

The focus area for this Map-a-thon is Kangaroo Island and regional Victoria.

name: United Nations for Mali - SOUTH ANSONGO: roads, waterways and villages
shortDescription:
**[Unite Maps](https://bit.ly/UniteMaps)** is a mapping initiative that aims to assist **[UN peacekeeping missions](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en)** in their field endeavors, such as **peace** and **security**, **navigation** and **logistics**, by providing its **peacekeepers** with **topographic maps** that will help them in their **tactical** and **operational activities**. 

 

In this project we will map topographic data, supporting **MINUSMA** to ensure peace in **Mali**. The features to add are: 

- **Roads** 

- **Waterways** 

- **Residential areas** 

- **Villages** 

 

**You are required to carefully read all the instructions inside the project before starting to map**. Ask any mapping or validation question in the **Questions and comments section** below. 

 

**[UN Mappers](https://bit.ly/UNMappers)** is a thriving community ranging from **UN personnel on the field** (GIS groups, UN offices, military and police) to **academia** (highschools and universities), from **local communities** and **NGOs** to **any remote volunteer** in the world. 
 

Don’t forget to follow our activities through our [social media](https://bit.ly/UNMappersSocialMedia) or [send us an e-mail](mailto:un.mappers@un.org) if you want to stay regularly updated on our mapping activities or to propose further engagements.

name: Missing Maps: Dakoussa, Takeita, Zinder, Niger
shortDescription: The Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre, Niger Red Cross Society and the French Red Cross, with funding from AFD and Cooperation Monegasque are implementing a project - to build the resilience of agro-pastoral communities in the Zinder region, Niger against food insecurity and nutrition crisis from Drought. Funding from the British Red Cross will support to expand the project. The data contributed will be used to assist in forecasting future disaster impacts, by knowing in advance where is likely to be impacted and its exposure and vulnerability. The information will help implementation of early action activities in response to a forecasted drought, before it occurs, contributing to reduce risk, prepare for effective response and ultimately to strengthen community resilience.

name: Missing Maps: Bangladesh Padma River Basin 4
shortDescription: The Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS) in partnership with the German Red Cross, Red Cross Red Crescent  Climate Centre, Department of Disaster Management and Flood Forecasting Warning Centre are implementing a project aimed at enabling communities prepare for the impacts of floods. name: Missing Maps: Buildings in Djibo, Burkina Faso (1)
shortDescription: In Burkina Faso, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) teams opened projects in the northern provinces of Soum and Oudalan in 2018, to increase the provision of emergency health care services and assist with other medical needs of the local and displaced communities. MSF supported three hospitals in Dori, Gorom-Gorom, and Djibo, reinforcing their emergency care capacity by training staff, rehabilitating buildings and operating theaters, and donating medical equipment and medicines. An updated map of Djibo will help the teams to understand the exact situation in the area and to make rough population estimations.

name: Refugee Site Mapping - Buramino Refugee Camp - Ethiopia
shortDescription:
Since 2017, CartONG and its community of volunteers have been involved in the mapping of several refugee camps that do not yet appear on any map. 

Currently the organizations in charge of these camps that ensure access to basic facilities and provide humanitarian aid don't have up-to-date maps on the areas in question. Once the map is completed remotely on OpenStreetMap, the operators in the field will add additional data on the infrastructures. The maps then created will be used for refugee camp planning  in order to improve the living conditions of the communities.

shortDescription:
GeoLab, chapter of YouthMappers and research laboratory of the Environmental School of the University of Antioquia, organizes this task to map the urban area and countryside divisions of the municipality of Dabeiba affected by landslides in the rainy season - Antioquia, Colombia.

On the night of Friday, November 13, there were heavy rains that generated several landslides and a torrential avenue in Dabeiba, western Antioquia, blocking the main highway and alternate roads.

This emergency, associated with the second rainy season, mainly affected the Dabeiba Viejo, El Cajón and Mohán countryside divisions. Some paths remain isolated and the terrain is difficult to access.
This natural disaster also leaves people affected, homes destroyed and damaged, three affected educational centers, as well as several kilometers of roads affected.

name: United Nations for Democratic Republic of the Congo - LUSAMBO: roads, waterways and villages
shortDescription:
**[Unite Maps](https://bit.ly/UniteMaps)** is a mapping initiative that aims to assist **[UN peacekeeping missions](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en)** in their field endeavors, such as **peace** and **security**, **navigation** and **logistics**, by providing its **peacekeepers** with **topographic maps** that will help them in their **tactical** and **operational activities**. 

In this project we will map topographic data, supporting **MONUSCO** to ensure peace in **Democratic Republic of the Congo**. The features to add are: 

- **Roads** 

- **Waterways** 

- **Residential areas** 

- **Villages** 

**You are required to carefully read all the instructions inside the project before starting to map**. Ask any mapping or validation question in the **Questions and comments section** below. 

**[UN Mappers](https://bit.ly/UNMappers)** is a thriving community ranging from **UN personnel on the field** (GIS groups, UN offices, military and police) to **academia** (highschools and universities), from **local communities** and **NGOs** to **any remote volunteer** in the world. 

Don’t forget to follow our activities through our [social media](https://bit.ly/UNMappersSocialMedia) or [send us an e-mail](mailto:un.mappers@un.org) if you want to stay regularly updated on our mapping activities or to propose further engagements.

name: Mapping Transport Networks for Accessibility in Bhutan
shortDescription: The World Bank’s Poverty and Equity Global Practice (ESAPV) is engaged in a series of projects in Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal to relate accessibility to key services to economic and welfare outcomes using the tools and concepts of economic geography. A foundational aspect of this work is modelling accessibility using geospatial analysis tools like network analysis and cost-time modeling, which model anticipated travel speeds over geospatial transport network datasets. High-quality, complete, and well-crafted transport network data is required for such models to return accurate results and is therefore critical to the overall success of these projects. Unfortunately, the World Bank ESAPV team has noted a number of errors, gaps, and omissions in the available transport network data for each country.

In order to implement relevant site improvement to reduce the flood risk in the area, an updated map is needed. Moreover, it will abound and help to design the emergency plans (settlement evacuation in case of massive floods) created with local communities.

name: Refugee Site Mapping - Sayam Forage - Niger
shortDescription:

Once the map is completed remotely on OpenStreetMap, the operators in the field will add additional data on the infrastructures. The maps then created will be used for refugee camp planning  in order to improve the living conditions of the communities.

name: United Nations for Central African Republic - NORTH BANGASSOU: roads, waterways and villages
shortDescription:
**[Unite Maps](https://bit.ly/UniteMaps)** is a mapping initiative that aims to assist **[UN peacekeeping missions](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en)** in their field endeavors, such as **peace** and **security**, **navigation** and **logistics**, by providing its **peacekeepers** with **topographic maps** that will help them in their **tactical** and **operational activities**. 

 

In this project we will map topographic data, supporting **MINUSCA** to ensure peace in **Central African Republic**. The features to add are: 

- **Roads** 

- **Waterways** 

- **Residential areas** 

- **Villages** 

 

**You are required to carefully read all the instructions inside the project before starting to map**. Ask any mapping or validation question in the **Questions and comments section** below. 

 

**[UN Mappers](https://bit.ly/UNMappers)** is a thriving community ranging from **UN personnel on the field** (GIS groups, UN offices, military and police) to **academia** (highschools and universities), from **local communities** and **NGOs** to **any remote volunteer** in the world. 
 

Don’t forget to follow our activities through our [social media](https://bit.ly/UNMappersSocialMedia) or [send us an e-mail](mailto:un.mappers@un.org) if you want to stay regularly updated on our mapping activities or to propose further engagements.

name: Missing Maps: Buildings, San Pedro Sula environs, Honduras - OLD
shortDescription:
This project is set up to support the MSF team in hurricane recovery and dengue prevention activities. 

In November 2020 central America was hit by two hurricanes named Eta and Iota. The two category four hurricanes caused landslides, flash flooding and destruction. In [this](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-55064560) article you can find more information and images of the damage. MSF is currently supporting the population in and around San Pedro Sula in general recovery from the hurricane's, but is especially also working to prevent an outbreak of dengue in the area. For this reason a precise mapping of all buildings in the area is needed. 

A first mapping in most of the areas has already happened for a [previous dengue response](https://www.msf.org/honduras-msfs-response-dengue-fever-emergency), and in direct reaction of the hurricanes. However to a check of the existing data and improvement of the data in certain neighbourhoods is needed to allow for exact prevention activities (literally every house that will be mapped will be checked and treated with larvicides by MSF teams!). This project will thus be only open for intermediate and advanced mappers.
author: Jorieke Vyncke

name: Mapping Transport Networks for Accessibility in Bhutan: Part 2
shortDescription: The World Bank’s Poverty and Equity Global Practice (ESAPV) is engaged in a series of projects in Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal to relate accessibility to key services to economic and welfare outcomes using the tools and concepts of economic geography. A foundational aspect of this work is modelling accessibility using geospatial analysis tools like network analysis and cost-time modeling, which model anticipated travel speeds over geospatial transport network datasets. High-quality, complete, and well-crafted transport network data is required for such models to return accurate results and is therefore critical to the overall success of these projects. Unfortunately, the World Bank ESAPV team has noted a number of errors, gaps, and omissions in the available transport network data for each country.

name: Fighting epidemics in precarious areas of Salvador, Brasil - Suburb I

name: Refugee Site Mapping - Kalma -  Sudan
shortDescription:
Since 2017, CartONG and its community of volunteers have been involved in mapping several displaced people camps and refugee camps that are not yet on any map. This project is about the mapping of Kalma camp in Sudan. 

Kalma camp in Sudan is an old camp dating from 2004, located a few kilometers from the city of Nyala, the capital of South Darfur. It hosts internally displaced persons (IDPs), i.e. people displaced within their own country. It was established following violent conflicts in the Darfur region.  In 2004, the camp housed about 40,000 people, today, more than 111,000 people live there. 
The United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR) has requested the help of CartONG and its community of volunteers to update the map on this site in order to have a better understanding of the current situation and to plan possible future extensions of the site. The camp is located in a flood-prone valley and is on major livestock migration routes.

name: United Nations for Somalia - MOGADISHU: buildings
shortDescription:
# **Read carefully the instructions before contributing to this project!**

**[Unite Maps](https://bit.ly/UniteMaps)** is a mapping initiative that aims to assist **[UN peacekeeping missions](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en)** in their field endeavors, such as **peace** and **security**, **navigation** and **logistics**, by providing its **peacekeepers** with **topographic maps** that will help them in their **tactical** and **operational activities**. 

In this **UN Mappers activation** we are going to map building footprints, supporting **UNSOS** to ensure peace in **Somalia**. The data will be used to deliver a **3D digital replica** of the city of **Mogadishu** to allow **peacekeepers** to remotely **visualize** and **analyze** inaccessible locations on the ground, **experience** different kind of scenarios beforehand, and **perform** operational planning around a shared simulated sandbox.

Take the chance of supporting peacekeepers by mapping Mogadishu urban area with the goal of producing a 3D model of the city! Height and roof information will be edited in a later stage on OSM. You will be able to check the results on https://osmbuildings.org/

**You are required to carefully read all the instructions inside the project before starting to map**. Ask any mapping or validation question in the **Questions and comments section** below or on our **[Discord server](https://discord.gg/bZRUdUpNxw)**!
author: Michael Montani

shortDescription:
# **Read carefully the instructions before contributing to this project!**

**[Unite Maps](https://bit.ly/UniteMaps)** is a mapping initiative that aims to assist **[UN peacekeeping missions](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en)** in their field endeavors, such as **peace** and **security**, **navigation** and **logistics**, by providing its **peacekeepers** with **topographic maps** that will help them in their **tactical** and **operational activities**. 

In this **UN Mappers activation** we are going to map building footprints, supporting **UNSOS** to ensure peace in **Somalia**. The data will be used to deliver a **3D digital replica** of the city of **Mogadishu** to allow **peacekeepers** to remotely **visualize** and **analyze** inaccessible locations on the ground, **experience** different kind of scenarios beforehand, and **perform** operational planning around a shared simulated sandbox.

Take the chance of supporting peacekeepers by mapping Mogadishu urban area with the goal of producing a 3D model of the city! Height and roof information will be edited in a later stage on OSM. You will be able to check the results on https://osmbuildings.org/

**You are required to carefully read all the instructions inside the project before starting to map**. Ask any mapping or validation question in the **Questions and comments section** below or on our **[Discord server](https://discord.gg/bZRUdUpNxw)**!

shortDescription:
Through this mapping task the Netherlands Red Cross supports the Malawi Red Cross Society to:
  - enhance resilience and building institutional disaster response capacity training for the people of Malawi

  - raise awareness within vulnerable communities in disaster prone areas of the possible dangers of natural disasters.

   - improve the delivery of sustainable water supply, sanitation and hygiene services in these low-income areas

   - respond to a food crisis to meet drought affected population’s food and nutrition needs through cash transfer.

Mapping efforts are coordinated with local government / members of the HOT/OSM community in Malawi.

The Missing Maps project aims to map the most vulnerable places in the world (affected by humanitarian crises: disease epidemics, conflict, natural disasters, poverty, environmental crises). name: Refugee Site Mapping - Adi Harush - Ethiopia
shortDescription:
Since 2017, CartONG and its community of volunteers have been involved in mapping several displaced people camps and refugee camps that are not yet on any map. This project is about the mapping of Adi-Harush camp in Ethiopia. 

In 2019 UNHCR - Ethiopia Operation in coordination with CartONG piloted a shelter and infrastructure mapping exercise in four refugee camps, Mai_Aini, Shimelba, Asayita and Kebribehya. Now they plan to scale up the shelter and infrastructure mapping to all of the remaining refugee camps. Mapping will support the data collection which will provide a basic map of the existing situation of each camps that can serve as a real time information and planning of interventions.

The Adi-Harush refugee camp was established in March 2010 to accommodate Eritrean refugees seeking international protection. Before the conflict erupted in the Tigray region in November 2020, the UNHCR had registered 32 000 refugees in Adi-Harush camp. Since the official announcement of the closure of Shimelba and Hitsats refugee camps by Ethiopia’s Government in late January, 3 600 refugees have relocated in Adi-Harush camp.

name: Adaptation and resilience of communities to climate change "SP Bolodou" Guinea
shortDescription:
Malgré le potentiel hydro-électrique de la Guinée évalué à environ 6 GW, il demeure cependant un pays fragile et vulnérable en matière d’atténuation aux impacts du changement climatique ainsi que sur les plans économiques et social.
C’est dans cette optique que le Bureau Pays Guinée appuie depuis 2017, des initiatives locales développées par les communautés de Bolodou et de Firadou (Préfectures de Guéckédou et Kissidougou en Guinée forestière) pour produire de l’énergie électrique par la construction de pico barrages hydro-électriques hors réseaux (PCH).
Pour ce faire, l’approche de la cartographie citoyenne, participative et libre du Projet OpenStreetMap a été nécessaire pour appuyer les initiatives dans la mise à disposition des données cartographiques de base dans la sous-préfecture de Bolodou.

name: Sanitation Mapping in Mpulungu
shortDescription:
Mpulunga town has been experiencing an influx of people in the recent past, a situation which has resulted in high pressure on the existing infrastructure especially related to waste management and sanitation. One of the major problems being faced in the district is that of poor sanitation, a problem which has existed for a long time now and one of the contributing factors to this problem is lack of adequate information on the status of sanitation within the township. Never has a project even been undertaken to ensure that sanitation is improved within the district despite the numerous challenges being faced. As a result, it is prudent that information should be made available, particularly information relating to the type of housing, status of roads, population density, number of households and proximity to existing sewer systems. Such information can only be made available once mapping of the existing buildings and roads is made available.

As a result, the remote mapping of buildings will help in providing the much-needed information to help in improving the sanitation situation in Mpulungu and probably for any other uses if need be.

name: Mapping Transport Networks for Accessibility inPakistan: Additional AOIs
shortDescription:
The World Bank’s Poverty and Equity Global Practice (ESAPV) is engaged in a series of projects in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, and Pakistan to relate accessibility to key services to economic and welfare outcomes using the tools and concepts of economic geography. A foundational aspect of this work is modelling accessibility using geospatial analysis tools like network analysis and cost-time modelling, which model anticipated travel speeds over geospatial transport network datasets. High-quality, complete, and well-crafted transport network data is required for such models to return accurate results and is therefore critical to the overall success of these projects. Unfortunately, the World Bank ESAPV team has noted a number of errors, gaps, and omissions in the available transport network data for each country.

For this purpose, the World Bank has contracted Kathmandu Living Labs (KLL) to observe and correct errors and missing transportation data in OpenStreetMap (OSM) of Pakistan. The main objective of this effort is to create missing transport data – principally road and path networks – in focus areas of interest (AOIs) provided by the World Bank in the form of polygonal shapefiles.

name: Refugee Site Mapping - Tongogara - Zimbabwe
shortDescription:
Since 2017, CartONG and its community of volunteers have been involved in mapping several displaced people camps and refugee camps that are not yet on any map. This project is about the mapping of Tongogara camp in Zimbabwe.


Established in 1981, the Tongogara refugee camp is located in the Chipinge district of Manicaland province. Initially the camp was an agricultural experiment station. The camp first opened for refugees fleeing the civil war in Mozambique. In the beginning of the 1990's it hosted up to 60,000 refugees from Mozambique. After the civil war ended in 1994, most refugees were repatriated. Conflicts in the Democatic Republic of Congo (DRC), Burundi, Rwanda, Angola, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Sudan and Uganda fuelled new influxes of the refugees from 1998 onwards. 
In July 2021, the Tongogara refugee camp was home to 15,151 people, many of whom were from DRC (UNHCR, 2021).
author: Eliot Sotty

name: IDEAMAPS Community mapping.
shortDescription:
With an annual growth rate of 4% annually, the population of African cities is rapidly growing. This growth has been accompanied by an increase in the number & population of informal settlements within these urban centers. Accurate data of the informal settlements is essential for developing a comprehensive roadmap for resilient and sustainable urban planning strategies by different stakeholders. The dearth of data on the informal settlement can be attributed to a lack of recognition by the city authorities due to their often illegal/squatting status. Detailed maps on the households and infrastructure of informal settlements are often non-existent. 
This exercise will focus on mapping buildings, road access, the available amenities, environmental risks, and the assets of the community within Korogocho informal settlement, home to over 150,000 residents and is located 8.5 km east of Nairobi city centre.
author: Zack Wambua

name: Refugee Site Mapping - Sheder - Ethiopia
shortDescription:
Since 2017, CartONG and its community of volunteers have been involved in mapping several displaced people camps and refugee camps that are not yet on any map. This project is about the mapping of Sheder camp in Ethiopia.   

In 2019 UNHCR - Ethiopia Operation in coordination with CartONG piloted a shelter and infrastructure mapping exercise in four refugee camps, Mai_Aini, Shimelba, Asayita and Kebribehya. Now they plan to scale up the shelter and infrastructure mapping to all of the remaining refugee camps. Mapping will support the data collection which will provide a basic map of the existing situation of each camps that can serve as a real time information and planning of interventions.

Established in 2008, Sheder Refugees camp is one of eight camps in the Somali region of Ethiopia hosting Somali refugees seeking international protection and asylum in Ethiopia. According to the UNHCR, Sheder camp hosted near 12 000 refugees in 2020.

name: Missing Maps: MSF/RCRC buildings in Kassala, Sudan
shortDescription:
Kassala is a city in the East of Sudan and facing simultaneously, multiple hazards: prone to flooding by the Mareb River, at risk of droughts, food insecurity, and historically impacted by conflict (further information: https://arcg.is/1eqOXj). The city is further home to refugees and internally displaced people, who fled from conflict and are most vulnerable. 

MSF and other actors like The Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre manage projects in this region, and detailed mapping will help to expand anticipatory action (acting before a disaster happens www.anticipation-hub.org/) to those most affected by conflict and climate.  Currently, the planning of early action is hampered by the lack of geospatial data in Sudan. Support actors like MSF and the RCRC Climate Centre to reach those most in need by mapping Kassala, providing crucial data and making the people living there visible on the world map!

name: Missing Maps: MSF/RCRC, updating buildings in Wad Sherifey refugee camp, Sudan
shortDescription:
NOTE: This is a building footprint update project.  There are already many buildings mapped, but due to various factors, the footprint has changed a lot in recent months.  This mapping project uses very recent satellite imagery from late August 2021, and is intended for intermediate/advanced mappers to update the building footprint.

Wad Sherifey is a refugee camp located in the East of Sudan along the Mareb River. During the past months a high number of refugees fleeing from conflict in Ethiopia has arrived and settled in the area, partly within flood prone areas of the Mareb River. Already vulnerable and displaced, now additionally facing the risk of floods. 

MSF and other actors like The Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre manage projects in this region, and detailed mapping will help to expand anticipatory action (acting before a disaster happens www.anticipation-hub.org/) to those most affected by conflict and climate. Support actors like MSF and the RCRC Climate Centre  to reach those most in need by mapping the Wad Sherifey camp and its surrounds to provide crucial information needed for the planning of early action and response in the area.

name: United Nations for Madagascar - VAKINANKARATRA: roads (3)
shortDescription:
**Carefully read the instructions before contributing to this project!** 

**First time on OpenStreetMap? Click [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zd5SN7eKKucS3-HDNsNvezoRhpWt7h6g/view?usp=sharing)!**

Ask any mapping or validation question in the **Questions and comments section** below. 

Going to school every day is not an easy ride for many students in the world. The [Ministry of Education in Madagascar](https://www.education.gov.mg/) is seeking to map the full road network (including trails and walking paths) in the Vakinankaratra region to make sure that the journey to school can be as straightforward as possible.  

The Ministry of Education is collaborating with Unite Maps and the UNESCO International Institute for Educational Planning (IIEP-UNESCO) in this **UN Mappers activation** to map missing tracks and paths to connect the full road network together. The road network produced will then be processed using the IIEP UNESCO [school catchment plugin](https://github.com/iiepdev/school-catchment-plugin), so that it will be possible to assess travel times children undertake every day from home to school, and to design better interventions in Vakinankaratra. 

**Take the chance of supporting education in Madagascar!**

shortDescription:
Those jamoats are part of the list of the most vulnerable of Tajikistan given by the Red Cross, where they take action. Tajikistan is one of the most climate-vulnerable countries in Central Asia, frequently experiencing natural disasters that take lives and destroy or degrade land, crops, and infrastructure, especially in remote villages in mountainous regions.

The project “Participatory Mapping in Tajikistan” funded by GIZ and jointly implemented by the NGO Little Earth and CartONG specifically focuses on creating maps and data for supporting disaster risk reduction and adaptation to climate change in remote, mountainous communities of Tajikistan.

shortDescription:
UNHCR Zambia Operation include 3 settlements (Mantapala, Mayukwayukwa, Maheba). Recently, Country Office expressed the need to have Camp Mapping Overview. This operation is preparing for a wide verification exercise and is very interested to most recent data in the camps.
The mapping of these sites will help the HCR having most recent camp data information and will then ease their effort of data collection.

According to the HCR, Mantapala refugee site has been set up in early 2018 as an integrated refugee settlement. This site enables refugees to develop their livelihoods and contribute to the local development of Nchelenge district, Luapula Province. Mantapala started receiving DRC refugees in January 2018. The majority of refugees have a farming, trading and artisan background. 
In November 2018, the HCR counted near 12 000 refugees in Mantapala.

shortDescription: Jama'are  LGA Bauchi has been listed as one of the highly probable flood risk LGA's in Nigeria .Flood is one of the major disasters ravaging  vulnerable communities in Nigeria .The Nigeria Hydrological Service Agency (NIHSA)  early this year  in an Annual Flood Outlook 2021 presentation  for early warning system  and monitoring  declared that  121 Local Government in 27 states of Nigeria would be highly  vulnerable to Flood Risk in 2021 . This means that beside the on-going COVID19 pandemic, malaria prevalence ,food insecurity ,banditry and terrorism ,lives and properties would be at risk in the coming months of high floods in these 121  flood vulnerable communities. Unique Mappers Network Nigeria  in collaboration with  SciStarter, YouthMappers Chapters  and Citizen Science Volunteers would be mapping  to help the government ,international organizations and humanitarian relief  respond to flood in these communities . Unique Mappers Network would be mobilizing 200 Volunteers for a Mapathon event to generate generate Open Map Data to help the government and international humanitarian organizations respond to Vulnerable Flood Communities to save lives and properties in Nigeria. name: Mapping and validation of Sainamaina Municipality
shortDescription:
As a part of the Booster grant by OpenMapping Hub- Asia Pacific to support the advancement of ongoing mapping and community building activities by the OSM Nepal community, we are remotely mapping and validating Sainamaina Municipality. 

Sainamina Municipality is located in the northwest of Rupandehi district in the Lumbini Province of Nepal. The municipality is about 15 km apart from Lumbini, the precursor of world peace and the birthplace of the Lord Gautam Buddha, on the foothills of the Manoram Chure hill. It is surrounded by Butwal Sub Metropolitan City in the ea, Badganga Municipality and Kapilvastu Municipality in west, Sitganga Municipality, Argakhanchi, Rainadevi, Chhara and Tinau Rural Municipality in north and Suddhodhan, Kanchan, Gaidhawaha Rural Municipality in the south. Sainamaina Municipality was formed by combination of Parroraha, Dudhrachya VDCs in 25thBaishak 2071 BS (May 8 2014 AD). Sainamaina Municipality consists of 11 wards. The total area of Sainamaina Municipality is 162.18 km2, According to census 2068(2011 AD) it holds 55822 populations and population density is 344.2 people per square kilometer.

We will be mapping 1.5 million people in OpenStreetMap (OSM) Nepal through the Booster Grant

name: Mapping and Validation of Bharatpur Metropolitan
shortDescription:
As a part of the Booster grant by OpenMapping Hub- Asia Pacific to support the advancement of ongoing mapping and community building activities by the OSM Nepal community, we are remotely mapping and validating  Bharatpur Metropolitan. 

Bharatpur is a city in the central-southern part of Nepal. Located in Chitwan District, Bharatpur is the district headquarter of the Chitwan District, as well as a separate Metropolitan authority, and is the fifth-largest city of Nepal with a population of 199,867 (census 2011). Bharatpur is one of the fast-growing cities of Nepal. It lies on the left bank of the Narayani River and serves as a commercial center of the Chitwan district and central region of Nepal. It is located at the center of Mahendra Highway and Kathmandu - Birganj (North-South) road corridor. The proximity of this city from Kathmandu (146 km), Pokhara (126 km), Butwal (114 km), Ghorahi (275 km), Birganj (128 km), Hetauda (78 km), and PrithiviNarayan (Gorkha) (67 km) has augmented the importance of its advantageous geographical location. In addition to good road access, Bharatpur has regular daily air services to Kathmandu and Pokhara

We will be mapping 1.5 million people in OpenStreetMap (OSM) Nepal through the Booster Grant

name: Rural development project - Jacmel and Bainet valley, Southeast of Haïti
shortDescription:
Le but de ce projet est de cartographier le bâti ainsi que le réseau routier dans les communautés rurales de la vallée de Jacmel et Bainet, situées au Sud-Est d’Haïti. Ce projet de cartographie est réalisé avec Habitat Cité Pantin qui possède un relais local sur le terrain : l’organisation locale OJUCAH (Organisation des Jeunes Universitaires de Carrefour pour l’avancement d’Haïti).

Grâce aux données collectées il sera possible de créer des cartes qui serviront à l’organisation locale Haïtienne. Elles permettront de mieux comprendre le territoire et d'obtenir des informations des populations et des pouvoirs publics afin de créer des moyens de communication et des outils de travail à destination des bailleurs de fonds. 

Les fonds de cartes produits et actualisés permettront également de référencer et partager les réalisations des projets, analyser les informations issues d’enquêtes, et dans un autre temps, référencer les zones à risques avec les habitants.

shortDescription:

The small town was reduced to rubble, timber and twisted metal with a large crater at the center of the explosion. As of January 26, 13 people had been confirmed dead and approximately 200 injured.
Responding to disasters of this nature is usually difficult in the absence of maps. The OSM Ghana community is calling on your mapping assistance to help plan and conduct further damage assessment and service delivery to those in need.

name: Muhanga Urban Mapping
shortDescription:
Project Specific Mapping Notes
Imagery: Please use Esri world imagery.

Many of these squares will already be partially or fully mapped, map in more if needed or fix up the existing mapping, or just mark it "Done" if it is already complete.

Existing mapping does not match imagery - This happens in some areas. Use the Esri world imagery, but adjust it so it aligns with the existing mapping, then continue mapping. Please leave a comment in the Tasking Manager when you mark done/stop mapping to say you adjusted the imagery.

Buildings
Please accurately outline all the buildings you can find. The outline should be for the full size of the building even if it is partly covered by trees in the imagery.
Take care to not include the building shadow in the building outline.
After drawing the outline and tagging as a building, use the 'Q' key in the iD web editor to "square" the corners.
Many buildings are very close, but do not actually touch each other, try to map them close to each other without letting them connect or share nodes with each other, roads or residential area outlines. In the iD web editor, holding down the "alt" key will keep nodes from "snapping" to each other and accidentally connecting.

shortDescription:
L’association des Originaire de Grande Plaine (AOG) est une association communautaire paysanne présente dans la commune de Gros Morne en Haïti. Elle travaille actuellement sur un programme visant à l’amélioration de l’accès à l’eau et à l’assainissement dans la localité de Grande Plaine. 

Dans le but de mieux comprendre la circulation de l’eau, l’origine de l'épuisement des sources et réfléchir à des solutions pour que l’accès à l’eau soit facilité pour tous, l'AOG aimerait avoir une carte détaillée de la zone car elle n’apparait même pas en tant que localité sur les cartes du monde et les ONG travaillant sur place manquent cruellement de données géographiques pour mieux intervenir. L'AOG déploie également des dispositifs individuels d'assainissement écologique et leur localisation géographique permettrait d'optimiser les filières de collecte et de traitement des résidus.

La cartographie de cette zone est donc très importante pour l’AOG, elle servira de support dans la prise de décision et permettra d’intervenir plus efficacement dans le cadre de ses activités.

Edificios: Muitos edifícios são muito próximos mas na verdade não se tocam. Tente mapeá-los o mais próximo possível, sem permitir que eles se conectem entre si ou com as ruas.

Para Incluir Estradas em Áreas onde não existem as Estradas mapeadas ainda, a Imagem que deve ser usada e a imagem de satelite atualizada "Maxar Premium" que servira de base para o mapeamento de novas estradas.

Ruas de serviço: Selecione a etiqueta "service" - ruas dentro de mercados, shoppings, escritórios / estações de serviço, etc.

Caminho para pedestre: Selecione a tag "footway" - caminhos acessíveis apenas a pé.

Área Verde "Mata Nativa ou Relfa": Selecione a tag "natural=wood" - Para Mata Nativa ou natural=wood para Relfa.

Ponto de Interesse: Clique no Botão Ponto e na Consulta ao Lado Esquerdo pesquise o que se quer ser mapeado; EX: ( Escola ).

Esses pontos de interesse podem ser mapeados através de conhecimento local ou dados da Prefeitura, Governo Estadual ou Governo Federal.

name: Refugee Site Mapping - Oure Cassoni - Chad
shortDescription:
The UNHCR operation in Chad has 21 camps. Mapping these sites will help UNHCR to have the most up-to-date information, which will facilitate its data collection efforts.

According to UNHCR, there are currently 1 079 221 refugees in Chad. The Oure Cassoni camp in Ennedi East province (the 5th largest refugee-hosting province in the country) opened in January 2004. It hosts 35 631 refugees (January 2022). The majority of them are from Sudan.

Posteriormente, outras áreas serão cadastradas para que todo o território municipal seja mapeado. O município fica no coração da Amazônia e apresenta grande biodiversidade e diversas populações tradicionais, porém devido aos riscos próprios e singularidades locais, como ineficiência ao acesso a internet aliado às grandes escalas da Amazônia dificultam a aquisição de dados pelo poder público.

# **Read carefully the instructions before contributing to this project!**

**[Unite Maps](https://bit.ly/UniteMaps)** is a mapping initiative that aims to assist **[UN peacekeeping missions](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en)** in their field endeavors, such as **peace** and **security**, **navigation** and **logistics**, by providing its **peacekeepers** with **topographic maps** that will help them in their **tactical** and **operational activities**. 

In this **UN Mappers activation** we are going to map building footprints, supporting **UNSMIL** to ensure peace in **Libya**. The data will be used to deliver a **3D digital replica** of the city of **Tripoli** to allow **peacekeepers** to remotely **visualize** and **analyze** inaccessible locations on the ground, **experience** different kind of scenarios beforehand, and **perform** operational planning around a shared simulated sandbox.

Take the chance of supporting peacekeepers by mapping Tripoli urban area with the goal of producing a 3D model of the city! Height and roof information will be edited in a later stage on OSM. You will be able to check the results on https://osmbuildings.org/

name: Water and Sanitation Mapping in Nakawa Division s' Informal Settlements Kinawataka.
shortDescription: Access to clean water and sanitation is a necessity and thus a human right essential to the dignity and safety of all people, however many people in Kampala’s informal settlements still lack access to safe drinking water and safely managed sanitation services. The inadequacy has led to severe outbreaks of fatal diseases like cholera, malaria etc. and women suffering the burden of collecting water from far places in these communities. The data collected from this project will help inform stakeholders of the difficulties and challenges faced by the residents, how to improve sanitation and determine areas where new water and sanitation facilities need to be constructed/installed.

name: Co-Mapper Tulum - Sustainable development - Quintana Roo
shortDescription:
The Co-Mapper Tulum project, driven by GFDRR and HOT, develops a pilot of a participatory local data creation methodology for municipal planning, as a first-of-its-kind OSM-project in Mexico and an opportunity to propose a systematized participatory approach to national authorities.

GEOID, HOT's specialized partner in Mexico, will carry out the full development of the project, the promotion of inter-institutional collaborative mapping and mapping with inhabitants, as well as the generation of the geospatial data visualization applications necessary for its use.
author: Céline Jacquin

name: Missing Maps: Lankien, South Sudan (1) DON'T USE
shortDescription:
In the past years in Jonglei state in northeastern South Sudan violence has erupted several times. These recurring episodes of intercommunal violence have devastating consequences for the population, the attacks cause displacement and loss of livelihoods for hundreds or even thousands of people. During the rainy season people are even more exposed to diseases like malaria, respiratory infections, and diarrhoea.

To try to answer the needs of the population MSF runs a primary healthcare centre in the town of Pieri and is currently exploring opening a new outreach site around the town. A better understanding of the geography and population numbers of Pieri and surrounding villages will help the MSF team to develop this new site.

In [this](https://blogs.msf.org/bloggers/bethany/bullets-wounds-bumpy-roads-and-bats-bed) blog MSF doctor Bethany Sampson shares about her time in Pieri.

name: Refugee Site Mapping - Lebanon
shortDescription:
Lebanon remains the country hosting the largest number of refugees per capita. With a population of 6,8 millions people, Lebanon hosts 1,5 millions Syrian refugees and some 13 700 refugees of other nationalities, according to the government.

The socio-economic downturn coupled with the COVID-19 pandemic and Beirut blast have all contributed to nine out of ten Syrian refugees living in extreme poverty.

The mapping of the main informal settlements in Lebanon for the UNHCR will help for emergencies preparedness in the future: fires, storms, floods, mass evictions.

name: Imagery for Social Good - Kuresoi North Subcounty Nakuru, Kenya
shortDescription: During the 2019-2020 pilot supported by Microsoft, 18 million building footprints were automatically extracted from satellite imagery for all of Tanzania and Uganda. HOT found that on average, mappers working without AI assistance could map between 1000-1500 buildings per working day. For areas with high-quality AI output, providing mappers with AI-generated building footprint suggestions increased this rate to up to 2500-3000 buildings per day (approximately doubling the rate at which building data could be added to OpenStreetMap, which is the crucial link for making it available to the humanitarian information management community).
author: DUNCAN KEBUT

name: Missing Maps: Lankien, South Sudan (1)
shortDescription:
In the past years in Jonglei state in northeastern South Sudan violence has erupted several times. These recurring episodes of intercommunal violence have devastating consequences for the population, the attacks cause displacement and loss of livelihoods for hundreds or even thousands of people. During the rainy season people are even more exposed to diseases like malaria, respiratory infections, and diarrhoea.

To try to answer the needs of the population MSF runs a primary healthcare centre in the town of Pieri and is currently exploring opening a new outreach site around the town. A better understanding of the geography and population numbers of Pieri and surrounding villages will help the MSF team to develop this new site.

In [this](https://blogs.msf.org/bloggers/bethany/bullets-wounds-bumpy-roads-and-bats-bed) blog MSF doctor Bethany Sampson shares about her time in Pieri.

shortDescription: On May 22nd, 2021, an eruption of the Nyiragongo volcano affected the neighbourhoods North of Goma and damaged more than a thousand houses. At the early hours of May 27th, after several days of repeated tremors, the provincial government requested inhabitants of 10 Goma neighbourhoods to evacuate the city. At that time the OSM community had updated the detailed mapping of the town of Rutshuru as it was one of the areas to which the inhabitants of Goma were evacuated. The present task aims at mapping in detail (buildings and roads) the surroundings of the city of Rutshuru.

Indeed, the commune does not have a communal map, nor a cadastral plan, which makes it difficult to carry out development projects, including tourist development. 

The OSM data produced will then be used to produce maps to better identify the villages, the boundaries between them, the main communication routes, and to locate the development projects already carried out, such as the drinking water supply to Mbadani.

name: Flooding in Old Fangak- South SUdan
shortDescription:
Jonglei, Unity, and Upper Niles remain the worst impacted states, with some 80 percent of the total cumulative number of affected people, the UN said. The situation is particularly bad in Jonglei State, where 305,000 people were affected, followed by Unity (220,000 affected) and Upper Nile (141,000 affected).

Access to the most vulnerable populations is a major impediment to humanitarian relief. Poor or no road infrastructure make it hard for external support to reach remote locations, such as Old Fangak, where the former airstrip is completely submerged and currently unusable for landing.

name: Mapping of refugee camps - Kouchaguine-Moura
shortDescription:
The UNHCR operation in Chad has 21 camps. The mapping of these sites will help UNHCR to have the most up-to-date information, which will facilitate its data collection efforts.

According to UNHCR, there are currently 1,079,221 refugees in Chad (January 2022). The Kouchaguine-Moura camp, which opened in February 2020, is located in Ouaddai province, which is the first province hosting the most refugees (146,890 refugees). The camp currently has 11,892 refugees (January 2022), mostly from neighbouring Sudan (UNHCR, January 2022). 

During January 2022, clashes broke out between communities in two refugee camps in Sudan. This event forced 4,500 Sudanese to cross the border into Chad. Between 2 and 11 February, some 209 households or 810 people were relocated to the Kouchaguine-Moura camp (UNHCR, February 2022)

name: Mapping of precarious neighborhoods - Phnom Penh - Cambodia
shortDescription:
CartONG supports the NGO Planète Enfants & Developpement, within the framework of the global project of Housing and Living conditions Improvement. 

Planète Enfants & Developpement is the result of a French NGO established in Cambodia in 1984 to help children following the Khmer Rouge genocide. It is also active in Vietnam, Burkina Faso and Nepal. PE&D's fields of action focus on building a healthy and dignified environment for disadvantaged children who are victims of violence and exploitation. Most of the NGO's projects focus on early childhood care and education.

As part of the wider Housing and Living Conditions Improvement project, 4 poor communities in Phnom Penh were identified. In order to better identify their needs and resources in terms of urban planning, two people from the organisation are carrying out a participatory urban diagnosis. 

The OSM data produced will be used to conduct this project to map the area and to better understand it.

**[Unite Maps](https://bit.ly/UniteMaps)** is a mapping initiative that aims to assist **[UN peacekeeping missions](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en)** in their field endeavors, such as **peace** and **security**, **navigation** and **logistics**, by providing its **peacekeepers** with **topographic maps** that will help them in their **tactical** and **operational activities**.

**[UN Mappers](https://bit.ly/UNMappers)** is a thriving community ranging from **UN personnel in the field** (GIS groups, UN offices, military and police) to **academia** (high schools and universities), from **local communities** and **NGOs** to **any remote volunteer** in the world. 


Don’t forget to follow our activities through our [social media](https://bit.ly/UNMappersSocialMedia) or [send us an e-mail](mailto:un.mappers@un.org) if you want to stay regularly updated on our mapping activities or to propose further engagements.

name: Imagery for Social Good - NINGI Part 01, Nigeria
shortDescription: During the 2019-2020 pilot supported by Microsoft, 18 million building footprints were automatically extracted from satellite imagery for all of Tanzania and Uganda. HOT found that on average, mappers working without AI assistance could map between 1000-1500 buildings per working day. For areas with high-quality AI output, providing mappers with AI-generated building footprint suggestions increased this rate to up to 2500-3000 buildings per day (approximately doubling the rate at which building data could be added to OpenStreetMap, which is the crucial link for making it available to the humanitarian information management community).

name: Imagery for Social Good - Ako LGA, Gombe State  Nigeria
shortDescription: During the 2019-2020 pilot supported by Microsoft, 18 million building footprints were automatically extracted from satellite imagery for all of Tanzania and Uganda. HOT found that on average, mappers working without AI assistance could map between 1000-1500 buildings per working day. For areas with high-quality AI output, providing mappers with AI-generated building footprint suggestions increased this rate to up to 2500-3000 buildings per day (approximately doubling the rate at which building data could be added to OpenStreetMap, which is the crucial link for making it available to the humanitarian information management community).

name: [Disaster Response] - Pakistan Flood 2022, Nasirabad District, Balochistan
shortDescription:
The floods caused by the monsoon rains since mid-June 2022 has affected Balochistan, Sindh, Gilgit-Baltistan, Punjab, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) provinces of Pakistan. According to the official figures (NDMA, SIT-REP No.076) the massive floods have so far claimed 1,061 lives and injured 1,575 people. The estimated number of affected people is around 30 million, and around 1 million houses are totally or partially damaged leaving behind millions in need of urgent shelter.”

name: Sanitation and Hygiene Scenario in the Slum Community: A Fieldwork Program on Shanti Nagar Slum, Chittagong, Bangladesh
shortDescription: The project will fill the data gap by addressing present sanitation services and hygiene conditions and their accessibility & availability in slum areas of Chittagong. To see the exact reasons behind the brutal unhygienic sanitation conditions of the latrine system in a low-income community, the southern part of the Shanti Nagar slum under the Chittagong City Corporation area has been selected. This specific slum has been chosen as an example to highlight the typical situation of the maximum slums in the Chittagong area, as most of the slums are facing the same problems. The main purposes of this project are to create & update the database of present structural & hygiene conditions of the latrines on the Openstreetmap (OSM) platform, to indicate vulnerable & unhygienic latrines within the selected area, to show the spatial distribution of sanitation facilities & to make the data available for the mass people, local and government organizations. The whole project will emphasize on database creation through the fieldwork & which will be done by the chapter members of CUSS YouthMappers. Such a move will lead to regulate well-planned sanitation facilities to improve the living environment of the slum community.

name: Les journées de la cartographie
shortDescription:
Ville frontalière de la Côte d’Ivoire au nord du pays, Ouangolodougou, est une ville aux multiples enjeux. Carrefour internationale, tous les voyages internationaux pour le nord y transitent. Avec la fermeture des frontières pour des raisons de covid 19, de nombreuses voies clandestines ont été mise sur place. Cette situation est source d’insécurité car il n’y pas de possibilité de contrôle. Mieux avec la menace terroriste grandissante au Mali et au Burkina Faso, la ville de Ouangolodougou, fait partie des zones rouge en termes de sécurité.
Une ville bien cartographiée pourrait aider à la prise de décision en cas d’urgence. Ce mapathon a pour objectif de cartographier les bâtiments, les routes et  l'occupation du sol afin de rendre plus visible Ouangolodougou.

**[UN Maps](https://bit.ly/UniteMaps)** is a mapping initiative that aims to assist **[UN peacekeeping missions](https://peacekeeping.un.org/en)** in their field endeavors, such as **peace** and **security**, **navigation** and **logistics**, by providing its **peacekeepers** with **topographic maps** that will help them in their **tactical** and **operational activities**. 

In this project we will map **waterways** supporting **UNSOS** to ensure peace in **Somalia**.
 

**You are required to carefully read all the instructions inside the project before starting to map**. Ask any mapping or validation question in the **Questions and comments section** below. 


**[UN Mappers](https://mappers.un.org/)** is a thriving community ranging from **UN personnel on the field** (GIS groups, UN offices, military and police) to **academia** (high schools and universities), from **local communities** and **NGOs** to **any remote volunteer** in the world. 


Don’t forget to follow our activities through our [social media](https://mappers.un.org/news/social-media) or [send us an e-mail](mailto:un.mappers@un.org) if you want to stay regularly updated on our mapping activities or to propose further engagements.

Área Verde "Mata Nativa ou Relfa": Selecione a tag "natural=wood" - Para Mata Nativa ou natural=wood para Relfa.

Nous analysons par exemple  la densité des constructions, la structuration du réseau routier,  le type d'occupation du sol/ la vocation du foncier (la saisie du landuse se fera dans un deuxième temps). name: Maleny Maps: Digital Base Map for DRR [Buildings]
shortDescription: **Goal: Develop a base map of roads and driveways in the Maleny area for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR).** Maleny communities are vulnerable to bushfires, landslides and flooding. This is compounded with a diminished capacity to take action within the neighbourhood due to an ageing population and absentee land and homeowners. The recent storm seasons seem to indicate an increase in climate related risk. Motivated by the recent COVID-19 pandemic and upcoming bushfire season, Maleny is eager to build local community capacity towards becoming a more safe, resilient and sustainable regional town. The communal use of OpenStreetMap offers the potential for both housebound, absentee and outdoor orientated community members to participate, through remote and field mapping.

name: Missing Maps: Mangochi district, Malawi (4)
shortDescription:
In the past years, Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) worked alongside the Ministry of Health in Malawi to respond to several emergencies. 

After tropical storm Ana hit Malawi in January 2022, the country experienced a widespread cholera outbreak. From March onwards, MSF teams set up cholera treatment units, where they treated patients with severe and moderate symptoms. In Mangochi district, MSF’s team has set up a 70-bed cholera treatment center and has also implemented community activities focused on access to clean water and hygiene, as most people living in the area have no other alternative than to drink water taken from the lake. 

Other activities include training local health care workers, conducting health promotion sessions and epidemiological surveillance activities, and supporting local authorities in running an oral cholera vaccination campaign. 

Please help us to map the Mangochi district to support MSF’s activities associated with the cholera outbreak.
author: Jorieke Vyncke

Mapping housing developments will aid in understanding the status quo and propose interventions.

shortDescription: The Colombian Red Cross (CRC) is collaborating with the Z Zurich Foundation to improve community resilience to flooding in several communities in Colombia under the Flood Resilience Project. The objectives include strengthening community resilience to floods and developing a community diagnosis using the Community Climate Resilience Measurement for Communities (CRMC) approach in three urban settings in the regions of Cundinamarca, Atlántico and Antioquia. name: Building and Road Mapping in Kalurata District of Sri Lanka
shortDescription:
Kalutara District is one of the 25 districts of Sri Lanka, the second level administrative division of the country. The district is administered by a District Secretariat headed by a District Secretary (previously known as a Government Agent) appointed by the central government of Sri Lanka. The capital of the district is the city of Kalutara .
Kalutara district is subjected to regular flooding particularly with heavy rains in the upper catchments areas of the Kaluganga, damaging houses, urban centers schools the roads network, home gardens, crops, industries and etc. As such inhabitants of this district have been badly affected by frequent floods. Their livelihood and social life have been disturbed. Objective of this project is map buildings and roads of Kalutara district and use as the input for the exposure mapping done by Disaster Management Centre, Sri Lanka.

shortDescription:

In collaboration with local authorities, school communities, principals, and stakeholders, the project will map the existing road networks and buildings using the tasking manager. 

The **goal** is to identify high-risk school and pedestrian zones and implement safety measures to eradicate traffic injuries. name: Missing Maps: Tandjile, Chad (2)
shortDescription:
Chad is a largely semi-desert country that is home to more than 17 million people. Despite being rich in resources, it suffers from inadequate infrastructure and internal conflict. The country is embroiled in a chronic health crisis, with repeated epidemics and nutrition crises, and some of the highest rates of infant, child and maternal deaths in the world. MSF teams focus on supporting women, children, and the large number of refugees from conflicts in neighbouring countries. 

Epidemics of measles are recurrent in Chad and measles are a leading killer of young children. Vaccination coverage is weak countrywide and many families, even those in urban areas, struggle to access paediatric care if their child falls sick. In spring 2023 a mass measles vaccination campaign took place in the Tandjilé region in Chad. The mapping data was however of such low quality and was not of great help. We ask thus your support to map the area so it can be used for any future intervention in the region. 

*3rd pass validation complete*

There are a number of colonies inside Pragatinagar, including Daldale, Dhaulagiri Tol, Chhatis Ghare, Salghari, Pragatinagar, Prithivi Nagar, Dharapani, Saat Ghare, Kuna Ghat, Gaidi, Gaidi ko Thap, Mukti Kshetra, Laxmipur, and Bhagawati Tol.

name: Complement to the official diagnosis of risk on the volcano Popocatépetl slides
shortDescription:
The National Center for Disaster Prevention (CENAPRED) has detected "235 exhalations accompanied by steam, volcanic gases and ash" between Friday and Saturday (19-20/05/2023).  CENAPRED has placed the volcanic alert traffic light at "yellow phase two". On Saturday, the volcano exploded again, pouring incandescent fragments over the slopes" and an "eruptive column close to three kilometers high (El País, 26 March 2023). 
HOT, in communication with the CENAPRED, has been informed that the operations are in process and do not require immediate data due to the lack of capacity during this phase to process them, but the need exists for a more detailed map of roads on the slopes of the volcano of buildings and buildings especially isolated, to continue with the prevention plan of Popocatepetl after the current response. 
OSM Mexico invites you to map this project by providing all roads, observable surface, and isolated buildings and buildings on the periphery of the localities in the area, as a priority, continuing with the complete localities.

name: Manatuto
shortDescription:
Manatuto is a city on the Indonesian part of Timor.  The Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre manage projects in this region, and detailed mapping will help to expand anticipatory action (acting before a disaster happens www.anticipation-hub.org/) and disaster response.  Currently, the planning of early action is hampered by the lack of up to date and complete geospatial data in this area. 

This project focuses on anticipatory mapping in Timor-Leste, aimed at enhancing preparedness for potential disasters. Through a comprehensive multi-hazard analysis conducted across the country, high-risk areas were identified, and prioritization was given to the mapping of these areas in OpenStreetMap (OSM). Among these high-risk areas is Manatuto, which is prone to flooding, landslides, and tsunamis. To effectively utilize OSM data for early actions planning in this region, it is essential to update and complete the building footprints. The generated data will then play a crucial role in anticipatory action plannings in Timor-Leste, ensuring better preparedness fort potential disasters.
Most roads in this area already mapped and in some parts also most of the the buildings. The image we use now is more recent. In the already mapped areas  not yet mapped.

name: Missing Maps: Tandjile, Chad (3)
shortDescription:
Chad is a largely semi-desert country that is home to more than 17 million people. Despite being rich in resources, it suffers from inadequate infrastructure and internal conflict. The country is embroiled in a chronic health crisis, with repeated epidemics and nutrition crises, and some of the highest rates of infant, child and maternal deaths in the world. MSF teams focus on supporting women, children, and the large number of refugees from conflicts in neighbouring countries. 

Epidemics of measles are recurrent in Chad and measles are a leading killer of young children. Vaccination coverage is weak countrywide and many families, even those in urban areas, struggle to access paediatric care if their child falls sick. In spring 2023 a mass measles vaccination campaign took place in the Tandjilé region in Chad. The mapping data was however of such low quality and was not of great help. We ask thus your support to map the area so it can be used for any future intervention in the region.

name: Pante-Makasar
shortDescription:
Pante-Makasar is the main town in the exclave Oecusse and is a municipality of Timor Leste, an independent state on the eastern part of the Island Timor. The Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre manage projects in this region, and detailed mapping will help to expand anticipatory action (acting before a disaster happens www.anticipation-hub.org/) and disaster response.  Currently, the planning of early action is hampered by the lack of up to date and complete geospatial data in this area. 

This project focuses on anticipatory mapping in Timor-Leste, aimed at enhancing preparedness for potential disasters. Through a comprehensive multi-hazard analysis conducted across the country, high-risk areas were identified, and prioritization was given to the mapping of these areas in OpenStreetMap (OSM). Among these high-risk areas is Pante-Makasar, which is prone to flooding, landslides, and tsunamis. To effectively utilize OSM data for early actions planning in this region, it is essential to update and complete the building footprints. name: Flood Preparedness and Response for Garsen Central Ward
shortDescription:
The Garsen Central ward is renowned as an area with susceptibility to flood incidents, thus classifying it as a high-risk zone. As a result of this, the residents of the ward are adversely affected during the rainy seasons by the impacts of floods manifested through displacement, disruption of livelihood (owing to destruction of cropland and loss of livestock) and emergence of water-borne diseases.

The remote mapping initiative aims to update map data within the area that can help inform both preparedness and response efforts. The Kenya Red Cross aims to use the data gathered to estimate the exposed population to the flood hazard and identify routes and alternative locations or shelters for potential evacuation. Additionally, flood evacuation maps will be developed and facilitate accessibility analysis for essential amenities based on the data collected and mapped.

This initiative was prompted by forecasts generated by models and expert evaluations, there is a notable indication pointing to the likelihood of an impending El Niño phenomenon during the October to December season of 2023. This prediction implies regions within the country receiving enhanced rainfall and carries the potential for significant repercussions and impact.

name: Brewerville - OSM Liberia Community Building
shortDescription:
The West and Northern Africa openmapping Hub (WNAH) is the Regional Hub of the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team that support and collaborate with OSM Communities operating in west and north Africa. 

OSM Liberia, a member of the regional communities was established to expand the workings of the WNAH through promoting and facilitating quality contributions to the OpenStreetMap Platform. Considering the financial challenges that hinder the functioning of the OSM Liberia community, the WNAH provided financial resources for the implementation of a short term project. The project runs for six month and is aim at growing the community, enabling the development of leadership skills of local leaders, supporting mentorship to community members, improving the governance of operation of the organizations, and broadening ways in which open mapping and data are used and advocated for at the local level. 

As part of the project activities, this demo task was created to facilate the OSM Training at four university-based YouthMappers Chapter in Liberia. Participants at the Training were taught how to create osm user accounts, how to map with ID editor and JOSM and to contribute to mapping tasks on the HOT tasking manager. Mapping on this project is restricted only to buildings and roads. The project was drawn from Commonwealth District, Montserrrado County which all form part of politicial district #17, few  kilometers away from the country's capitol, Monrovia.
