name: Flood Preparedness and Response for Sabena Ward, Kenya
shortDescription:
Sabena ward, Garissa County is renowned as an area with a historical susceptibility to flood incidents, thus classifying it as a high-risk zone. As a result of this, the residents of the ward are adversely affected by the impacts of floods manifested through displacement, disruption of livelihood (owing to destruction of cropland and loss of livestock) and emergence of water-borne diseases.

The remote mapping initiative aims to update map data within the area that can help inform both preparedness and response efforts. The Kenya Red Cross aims to use the data gathered to estimate the exposed population to the flood hazard and identify routes and alternative locations or shelters for potential evacuation. Additionally, flood evacuation maps will be developed and facilitate accessibility analysis for essential amenities based on the data collected and mapped.

This initiative was prompted by forecasts generated by models and expert evaluations, there is a notable indication pointing to the likelihood of an impending El Niño phenomenon during the October to December season of 2023. This prediction implies regions within the country receiving enhanced rainfall and carries the potential for significant repercussions and impact.

shortDescription:

Map missing roads in the Kalikot district to help identify areas that are hardest to reach. The Kalikot district's local initiative provides valuable data for disaster risk reduction. 

[KIRDARC](https://kirdarc.org/), [Start Fund Nepal](https://startnetwork.org/funds/national-start-funds/start-fund-nepal), and AP Hub have taken the lead in initiating and coordinating the effort to map this specific area. You can grab all the OSM highway data in Kalikot using [this query](https://overpass-turbo.eu/s/1CFJ) and export it to your preferred data format.

The remaining parts of the Kalikot mapping project are projects 14422, 14423, 14424, and 14425.

shortDescription:

It claimed several lives, causing widespread damage as roads, bridges, and homes were washed away.
The Teesta River took a furious form, and part of the state's biggest hydropower project, Sikkim Urja, was washed away, exacerbating the situation.

Rescue operations remain a major challenge due to mudslides, washed-out roads, and damage to communication systems.

OSM North East, OSM India and GREd Foundation shall go ahead and map the areas which have been inundated by floods.

name: Earthquake Response in Herat, Afghanistan 2023 - ROADS
shortDescription:
A powerful 6.3-magnitude earthquake has struck western Afghanistan, just over a week after strong quakes and aftershocks killed thousands of people and flattened entire villages in the same region.

The US Geological Survey said the latest quake’s epicentre was about 21 miles (34km) outside Herat, the provincial capital, and the focus was 5 miles below the surface.

The aid group Doctors Without Borders said two people were reported dead while Herat regional hospital received more than 100 people injured in Sunday’s quake. Earthquakes on 7 October flattened whole villages in Herat, one of the most destructive quakes in the country’s recent history.

The initial quake, numerous aftershocks, and a second 6.3-magnitude quake on Wednesday flattened villages, destroying hundreds of mud-brick homes that could not withstand such force. Schools, health clinics, and other village facilities also collapsed.

Besides rubble and funerals after that devastation, there was little left of the villages in the region’s dusty hills. Survivors are struggling to come to terms with the loss of family members and in many places, living residents are outnumbered by volunteers who come to search the debris and dig mass graves.

(https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/oct/15/earthquake-strikes-afghanistan-region-still-reeling-from-week-of-devastation)

name: Akosombo Dam Spillage-Flood Mapping [1] #Mepe #Battor.
shortDescription:
[OpenStreetMap Ghana](https://osmghana.org/) in collaboration with [Tomtom](https://www.tomtom.com/), [Mobile Web Ghana](https://mobilewebghana.org/) and [Africa Open Data and Internet Research Foundation](https://aodirf.info/) are holding a mapping campaign to digitalise communities along the banks of the Volta Lake in the Volta Region of Ghana are flooded and in distress due to the opening of the Akosombo Dam and submerged in water. The Volta River Authority (VRA) began spilling water from the Akosombo Dam about October 15, 2023, in order to protect the dam from overtopping.
The influx of water has raised Volta levels, causing flooding in low-lying areas along the river, including, but not limited to, Mepe, Battor, Sogakope, Mafi, Adidomeand Ada…. According to the [National Disaster Management Organization (NADMO)](https://www.gbcghanaonline.com/general-news/mepe-grapples/2023/) in Ghana, more than 26,000 people have been displaced by floods in Mepe and other parts of North Tongu district and Nadmo is working with other organizations to provide assistance to affected residents. The Mepe floods are a reminder of the importance of disaster preparedness and response. It also serves as a reminder of the need to mitigate the impacts of climate change, which is making extreme weather events more common and severe.

Ce programme visera à investir dans des organisations qui amélioreront les contributions cartographiques pour permettre la mise à l'échelle des contributions locales à OpenStreetMap (2) et aux données géographiques ouvertes. OpenStreetMap est une base de données géographique gratuite et ouverte mise à jour et maintenue par une communauté de bénévoles via une collaboration ouverte. Le programme créera un cadre culturel guidé par des valeurs et des normes permettant une collaboration mondiale, qui comprendra des méthodes de travail et des mécanismes d'évaluation pour évaluer dans quelle mesure HOT et son personnel illustrent leurs propres valeurs fondamentales. Il sera lié aux thèmes prospectifs « au-delà de la localisation » en impliquant des groupes clés sous-représentés et en mettant en relation des partenaires dans une nouvelle région. Contribue au thème prospectif de la vulnérabilité climatique en raison des risques accrus auxquels sont confrontés les petits pays insulaires face aux événements liés au changement climatique.
L'objectif principal de ce programme est de fournir une formation spécifique et ciblée et un renforcement des capacités aux femmes et aux organisations locales issues de zones géographiques sous-représentées à haut risque (petites îles).
author: Mohamet Lamine Ndiaye

shortDescription:
MSF has been working in Kenya since 1987, providing medical services including treatment for HIV, TB and non-communicable diseases. In Homa Bay MSF is working on ensuring continuity of care for people with chronic diseases. MSF operates in Homa Bay’s state-run hospital where around 250 patients from all over the region are admitted every month. MSF works as well to enhance community initiatives by proposing differentiated care models based on a person-centered approach. Better maps will serve the MSF team to improve the understanding of patient origin and will facilitate and rationalize home visits to chronic disease patients.

name: MEXICO GUERRERO Recovery from Hurricane Otis 2023
shortDescription:
Hurricane Otis caused at least 27 deaths and severe damage when it struck the coast of the city of Acapulco, Mexico, as a Category 5. It is one of the fastest intensifying tropical cyclones on record, second only in the current era to Hurricane Patricia in 2015. While the authorities organize the action strategy on site, and post-disaster images are being produced, we are mapping the area of greatest impact around the city of Acapulco: buildings and roads. 
This project is organized by HOT's LAC Hub in articulation with CENAPRED. The mapping strategy will follow this collaboration.

name: Akosombo Dam Spillage-Flood Mapping [2] #Adidome  #Todze #New Bakpa
shortDescription:
[OpenStreetMap Ghana](https://osmghana.org/) in collaboration with [Sambus Geo Spatial Ghana](https://sambusgeospatial.com/),  [Tomtom](https://www.tomtom.com/), [Mobile Web Ghana](https://mobilewebghana.org/) , [Africa Open Data and Internet Research Foundation](https://aodirf.info/) and all [YouthMapper Ghana Chapters](https://www.youthmappers.org/) are holding a mapping campaign to digitalise communities along the banks of the Volta Lake flooded and in distress due to the opening of the Akosombo Dam and submerged in water. The Volta River Authority (VRA) began spilling water from the Akosombo Dam about October 15, 2023, in order to protect the dam from overtopping.
The influx of water has raised Volta levels, causing flooding in low-lying areas along the river, including, but not limited to, Mepe, Battor, Sogakope, Mafi, Adidomeand Ada…. According to the [National Disaster Management Organization (NADMO)](https://www.gbcghanaonline.com/general-news/mepe-grapples/2023/) in Ghana, more than 30,000 people have been displaced by floods in North Tongu district and NADMO is working with other organizations to provide assistance to affected residents. The Mepe floods are a reminder of the importance of disaster preparedness and response. It also serves as a reminder of the need to mitigate the impacts of climate change, which is making extreme weather events more common and severe.

author: Stephen Mawutor Donkor

name: Palestine -Innovation - Nablus1
shortDescription:
El proyecto de Cruz Roja Española en el que están enmarcadas estas tareas, se encuentra en Palestina, una zona propensa a las catástrofes naturales, sobre todo a los terremotos debido a la gran actividad sísmica del Mar Muerto. 

Además, el pueblo palestino se enfrenta a inundaciones repentinas, sequías y desertificación, así como a condiciones meteorológicas extremas, agravado por el rápido crecimiento de la población en las zonas urbanas.

En este contexto la Cruz Roja Española apoya a la Media Luna Roja Palestina, creando capacidades en las comunidades así como mejorando el entendimiento de la cultura del riesgo.

-	Estas tareas están enmarcadas en un proyecto a largo plazo.
-	En este proyecto se van a mapear **SOLO edificios**. 
-	El editor que vamos a utilizar es el ID-Editor.
-	Las imágenes satelitales a usar son **Bing Mapas Aérea**.

shortDescription:
In 2019-2020 the MSF team in Moissala, Chad organised a community and population estimation survey in the health district of Moissala to support a new maternal and child health programme. Thanks to the mapping of Missing Maps volunteers the technique of spatial sampling could be used to conduct the survey, and an accurate population estimation that was based on combining the survey data and building footprint data was made possible. 

Now, several years later, MSF teams are still working in the region and have requested for Missing Maps volunteers to update the building footprint data so they can update their population estimations and plan health activities accordingly.

shortDescription: In Sipili, a dynamic town in Laikipia County once known for its farm produce trade, the Arid Lands Information Network (ALIN) is spearheading a transformative initiative. Utilizing the "Beyond the Map grant," ALIN is developing base layers for Sipili, focusing on using GIS and open mapping tools for a critical mission: conducting suitability analysis for the optimal placement of community network masts. This project goes beyond traditional mapping, aiming to empower the community with enhanced digital connectivity. By carefully analyzing geographical data, ALIN seeks to identify the most effective locations for these masts, thereby ensuring robust network coverage and opening up new avenues for information access, humanitarian support, and innovation. This endeavor is a key step in integrating Sipili into the global digital community, marking a significant advancement in the town's journey towards a connected and technologically empowered future.

shortDescription: Kasama district is among the oldest districts in Zambia, and many areas lagged in terms of development. However, the cause has been described by many researchers to be poverty, education, access to basic needs, lack of road networks, etc. Therefore, mapping the local communities will help in fostering development agendas by connecting these communities to national development through open mapping. To help this district develop, we want to first map small communities that are made up of the districts and connect them to the national development through mapping. Lastly, the mapping of areas in this district will enhance sustainable development through effective planning by the local authorities.

name: El wak Flood Response Mapathon
shortDescription:
El wak area, Mandera County is renowned as an area with a historical susceptibility to flood incidents, thus classifying it as a high-risk zone. Due to the recent enhanced rainfall of the October- November- December 2023 season, the area has been adversely affected. As a result of this, the residents of the area area adversely affected by the impacts of floods manifested through displacement, disruption of livelihood (owing to destruction of cropland and loss of livestock) and emergence of water-borne diseases.

The remote mapping initiative aims to update map data within the area that can help inform response efforts. The Kenya Red Cross aims to use the data gathered to estimate the exposed population to the flood hazard and identify routes and alternative locations or shelters for potential evacuation. Additionally, flood evacuation maps will be developed and facilitate accessibility analysis for essential amenities based on the data collected and mapped.

In the past, mining has posed a variety of potential hazards to the local community, culminating in a fatal collapse in the 1980’s. In 2023, areas of Val-d’Or were also evacuated in response to encroaching wildfires and poor local air quality. 

This project aims to improve the base map and enable the addition of addresses to local buildings once mapped to bolster preparedness and aid in community lead response.

name: Missing Maps: Update Moissala health district, Chad (10)
shortDescription:
In 2019-2020 the MSF team in Moissala, Chad organised a community and population estimation survey in the health district of Moissala to support a new maternal and child health programme. Thanks to the mapping of Missing Maps volunteers the technique of spatial sampling could be used to conduct the survey, and an accurate population estimation that was based on combining the survey data and building footprint data was made possible. 

Now, several years later, MSF teams are still working in the region and have requested for Missing Maps volunteers to update the building footprint data so they can update their population estimations and plan health activities accordingly.

*3th pass validation done*

name: Eco Smart City Nigeria-Iseyin_1
shortDescription:
The Eco-Smart Cities project aims to tackle the complex issues in urban centers within the region. It envisions a future where cities become lively and intelligent ecosystems. The project aims to address environmental degradation, limited resources, inadequate infrastructure, public health concerns, and economic inequalities through a comprehensive, open data and participatory mapping approach. This project will stimulate sustainable urban growth that benefits current and forthcoming generations. This will be achieved by collecting data, conducting analyses, and presenting information visually. This valuable data will aid city planners, national authorities, the private sector, and other stakeholders in making informed decisions and shaping urbanization strategies.
To address the challenges related to sustainability, a comprehensive strategy that considers the environmental, social, and economic dimensions is required. Data can play a crucial role in this process. Still, it is essential to ensure that all stakeholders - including governments, local authorities, and private sector partners - collaborate effectively to develop and implement sustainable policies. One of the initial steps in this journey is to accurately map the city's layout, including its structures, buildings, amenities, roads, waterways, and land use.

shortDescription:
The South Sudan Red Cross is working on an Enhanced Vulnerability and Capacity Analysis (EVCA) together with the local communities, to assess and analyse the risks the communities face, explore where these risks come from, which members of the communities are most exposed, what coping capacities are available, and what initiatives can be undertaken to strengthen coping capacities and reduce the risks. 
The OpenStreetMap data will be used in the usage context of the [Sketch Map Tool](https://sketch-map-tool.heigit.org/) to orientate on the map and to collect spatial knowledge together with the communities.

name: Mapping Buildings in Cibitoke, Burundi
shortDescription:
The Cibitoke province of Burundi saw intense rainfall, high winds and flooding in October and December 2023.  Further, above average rainfall has been forecasted throughout the country.  

To support the local and international response to this disaster, the USAID mission has requested updated information on building data.  This project aims to start updating Cibitoke's building dataset.

name: DRC Congo River floods response
shortDescription:
The heavy rains that began in mid-November 2023 intensified until January 2024, causing major flooding in at least 18 of the Democratic Republic of Congo's 26 provinces. This year, the rising waters of the Congo River reached their highest level for more than 60 years, according to the Régie des voies fluviales.
To date, more than 430,000 households, or 2.1 million people, have been affected, according to official estimates.
The extent of the disaster remains difficult to assess accurately. However, the assessments carried out so far by humanitarian partners in certain provinces, notably Tanganyika, Kasai and the capital Kinshasa, reveal more or less the scale of the crisis:
More than 11,000 households (79,000 people) affected in the capital Kinshasa.
More than 50 per cent of the drinking water supply system destroyed in Kasaï and Tshopo provinces.
31 schools destroyed and more than 4,300 hectares of agricultural fields devastated in Tanganyika province.
Everywhere, the needs are immense. Thousands of families have lost everything. Epidemiological risks are heightened by overcrowding in the affected areas. Food, shelter, access to water and healthcare are absolute priorities.
Across the country, the Congolese authorities estimate that the torrential rains have damaged at least 98,299 homes and caused almost 300 deaths.

name: Open Mapping 4 Resilience : Mirpur, Dhaka District, Bangladesh
shortDescription:
**Strengthening Resilience Of Dhaka’s Slums Against Climate and Anthropogenic Hazards**

The population of Dhaka City has been steadily increasing, primarily fueled by domestic migration, including from coastal communities affected by climate hazards like tropical cyclones and other causes. Consequently, the city has witnessed a surge in slum areas and dwellers. It has strained the city's infrastructure, creating challenges for housing, sanitation, and basic amenities. Most slum areas are in high-risk disaster zones, including locations near riverbanks, low-lying areas, and polluted water sources. Swamp dwellers face frequent risks such as river overflow, clogged floods, urban heat, and settlement fires. Over the years, slum settlements have expanded, encroaching upon vacant government land, reclaimed water bodies, and shallow wetlands.

This phenomenon underscores the complex interplay between climate-induced displacement and urbanization, emphasizing the need for sustainable urban planning and resilience strategies to address the evolving demographic landscape in Dhaka. This is a challenge for the City Government and related parties. The availability of data and maps can help city governments provide information on infrastructure needs and basic services the community needs, especially the most vulnerable community groups (children, women, people with disabilities, and the elderly).

name: Missing Maps: Mini Maps - Rainbow Lake, AB, Canada
shortDescription:
This project is part of the initial trail run for the Mini Maps project series, a contributor to larger Missing Maps initiatives. If you're viewing this project, you should be a part of the Canadian Red Cross Team.

Mini Maps aims to target smaller, rural communities that often don't meet the requirements to be part of a larger Missing Maps initiative, but still need mapping.

Please prioritize mapping buildings - major roads can be added if needed. 

Rainbow Lake, located in Northwest Alberta, hosts a population of approximately 800 people. The town was evacuated during the 2023 wildfire season due to the long lake fire which had burned ~135,000 hectares of forest as of June 1, 2023. Thankfully, no homes in Rainbow lake were damaged during that event, but major fires continue to be present in the area.

name: DRC Congo River floods response
shortDescription:
The heavy rains that began in mid-November 2023 intensified until January 2024, causing major flooding in at least 18 of the Democratic Republic of Congo's 26 provinces. This year, the rising waters of the Congo River reached their highest level for more than 60 years, according to the Régie des voies fluviales.
To date, more than 430,000 households, or 2.1 million people, have been affected, according to official estimates.
The extent of the disaster remains difficult to assess accurately. However, the assessments carried out so far by humanitarian partners in certain provinces, notably Tanganyika, Kasai and the capital Kinshasa, reveal more or less the scale of the crisis:
More than 11,000 households (79,000 people) affected in the capital Kinshasa.
More than 50 per cent of the drinking water supply system destroyed in Kasaï and Tshopo provinces.
31 schools destroyed and more than 4,300 hectares of agricultural fields devastated in Tanganyika province.
Everywhere, the needs are immense. Thousands of families have lost everything. Epidemiological risks are heightened by overcrowding in the affected areas. Food, shelter, access to water and healthcare are absolute priorities.
Across the country, the Congolese authorities estimate that the torrential rains have damaged at least 98,299 homes and caused almost 300 deaths.

shortDescription: The work of the Canadian Red Cross in our domestic Missing Maps initiative centres around improving the basemap for communities at risk of disaster. Timmins, located on the traditional territory of the Mattagami First Nation in what is now Northeastern Ontario, is an area historically reliant on gold mining and resource extraction, posing potential environmental risks to the surrounding communities. Wildfires also pose potential risks to this area due to the surrounding dense forest, and seasonal flooding from the Mattagami River is also a concern. name: Missing Maps: Bentiu, South Sudan (1)
shortDescription:
Flooding has been an issue in South Sudan for many years, exacerbated by climate change. During the rainy season, floodwaters swept away entire villages, destroyed crops, drowned cattle and severely damaged infrastructure, while forcing hundreds of thousands of people from their homes. Last year, a larger than ever portion of South Sudan was covered in water, and in some places the floodwaters have still not receded. The past year has also seen a considerable influx of refugees fleeing the conflict in Sudan. 

In Bentiu, Unity state, the camp for displaced people is effectively an island protected by dykes. For aid organisations such as MSF, reaching people in need becomes increasingly difficult as floods sweep away or cover roads, bridges and airstrips. Please help us map Bentiu, so that MSF teams can more effectively access communities and help them to prepare for the rainy season, while ensuring that they can still access medical care.

name: Reserva Natural Bosawas - Nicaragua, Mapa Base 2024 (2)
shortDescription:
Bosawás en Nicaragua, con sus 2,042,535 hectáreas, es un componente indispensable del Corredor Biológico Mesoamericano. Posee 21 ecosistemas y seis tipos de bosques, no solo rica en biodiversidad, sino también en cultura, albergando poblaciones indígenas como la Miskitu y Mayagna. Hasta el año 1987 se tenía contabilizado que del tamaño total de la zona 1,604,683 hectáreas correspondían a bosques, pero entre los años 1987 – 2010 (23 años) se ha reportado que solo quedan 1,039,945 hectáreas de este a causa de la deforestación impulsada por la migración interna de personas desde la Región Pacifico del país en la búsqueda de tierras fértiles y espaciosas donde se pueda impulsar la franja ganadera y agrícola, así como el instalar asentamientos ilegales. 

El principal objetivo de este proyecto es crear un mapa base actualizado con la situación actual del despale constante en la Reserva de Biósfera Bosawás en Nicaragua, para documentar su daño a manos de colonos en el afán de agrandar la frontera agrícola y ganadera en la zona.

name: Missing Maps: Buildings in Sokoto, Nigeria (1)
shortDescription:
Since 2014, Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has been supporting aid in Sokoto, Nigeria. Particularly the Sokoto Noma Hospital, with a programme of activities for people affected by noma, including noma survivors and their families. Noma, a neglected and little-known non-contagious disease, mostly affects children under five living in poverty.

It starts as an inflammation of the gums, similar to a small mouth ulcer. In just two weeks the infection starts to destroy bone and tissue, potentially affecting the jaw, lips, cheeks, nose or eyes, leaving survivors with physical consequences including pain, breathing complications and difficulties eating. Noma has a strikingly high mortality rate, and those who do survive are left with life-changing facial disfigurements.

Four times a year, a team of international surgeons, anaesthesiologists and nurses travel to Sokoto Noma Hospital to operate on noma survivors. The hospital, run in collaboration with the Nigerian Ministry of Health, also focuses on community outreach, active case finding in the region, health promotion and mental health support. Better maps are needed in particular to support these community health activities.

To learn more about the noma disease you can check out [this page](https://noma.msf.org/).

name: Missing Maps: Buildings in Sokoto, Nigeria (3)
shortDescription:
Since 2014, Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has been supporting aid in Sokoto, Nigeria. Particularly the Sokoto Noma Hospital, with a programme of activities for people affected by noma, including noma survivors and their families. Noma, a neglected and little-known non-contagious disease, mostly affects children under five living in poverty.

It starts as an inflammation of the gums, similar to a small mouth ulcer. In just two weeks the infection starts to destroy bone and tissue, potentially affecting the jaw, lips, cheeks, nose or eyes, leaving survivors with physical consequences including pain, breathing complications and difficulties eating. Noma has a strikingly high mortality rate, and those who do survive are left with life-changing facial disfigurements.

Four times a year, a team of international surgeons, anaesthesiologists and nurses travel to Sokoto Noma Hospital to operate on noma survivors. The hospital, run in collaboration with the Nigerian Ministry of Health, also focuses on community outreach, active case finding in the region, health promotion and mental health support. Better maps are needed in particular to support these community health activities.

To learn more about the noma disease you can check out [this page](https://noma.msf.org/).

name: Eco Smart City Nigeria-Sagamu & Environs
shortDescription:
The Eco-Smart Cities project aims to tackle the complex issues in urban centers within the region. It envisions a future where cities become lively and intelligent ecosystems. The project aims to address environmental degradation, limited resources, inadequate infrastructure, public health concerns, and economic inequalities through a comprehensive, open data and participatory mapping approach. This project will stimulate sustainable urban growth that benefits current and forthcoming generations. This will be achieved by collecting data, conducting analyses, and presenting information visually. This valuable data will aid city planners, national authorities, the private sector, and other stakeholders in making informed decisions and shaping urbanization strategies.
To address the challenges related to sustainability, a comprehensive strategy that considers the environmental, social, and economic dimensions is required. Data can play a crucial role in this process. Still, it is essential to ensure that all stakeholders - including governments, local authorities, and private sector partners - collaborate effectively to develop and implement sustainable policies. name: Emergency basemaps for Myanmar - Gwa Township
shortDescription:
Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as myOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. You can contribute by mapping rivers, water bodies, roads, settlements, and other identifiable topographic features based on satellite imagery. To your mapped data we will add local knowledge such as river and village names, schools, clinics, and other important landmarks where available.

**The goal is to map critical information needed for emergency basemaps covering larger areas in a complete, accurate and reliable way** - such as access roads, villages and settlement areas, rivers and bridges to be used for operational basemaps maps covering whole townships. 
*The goal is NOT to map every minute feature*  We don't aim to map small creeks, individual houses, temporary tracks & paths, detailed landcover etc. but all important features for humanitarian action.
Your efforts will make it possible to map such larger areas with the required level of accuracy and turn those into much needed basemaps for Myanmar and its people.

A comunidade brasileira do OpenStreetMap e do YouthMappers estão coordenando uma campanha de mapeamento colaborativo de acessos a locais que encontram-se isolados para apoiar autoridades e a comunidade.

shortDescription: Le projet Eco-Smart Cities vise à résoudre les problèmes complexes des centres urbains régionaux en créant des écosystèmes urbains intelligents et vivants. L'objectif est de favoriser une croissance urbaine durable au bénéfice des générations actuelles et futures en collectant, analysant et visualisant des données précieuses pour les urbanistes, les autorités nationales, le secteur privé et d'autres parties prenantes. Pour relever les défis de la durabilité, une stratégie globale prenant en compte l'environnement, le social et l'économique est essentielle, avec la nécessité d'une collaboration efficace entre les gouvernements, les autorités locales et le secteur privé. Une première étape consiste à cartographier précisément la structure de la ville, y compris ses bâtiments, ses routes et son utilisation des terres.

name: Settlement Areas for Emergency basemaps - Thabaung Township
shortDescription:
Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as MyOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. 

You can contribute by **mapping and updating settlement areas** based on satellite imagery. Your settlement areas will be complemented by roads, rivers and points of interests mapped through HOT tasks that will follow. 

Knowing where people live is essential to prepare for emergency assistance and to access those people and provide help when needed.

Your efforts contribute to map larger areas with the required level of accuracy and turn those into much needed basemaps for Myanmar and its people.

name: Afghanistan 2024 Floods - Baghlan District - Map Roads (1/5)
shortDescription:
Heavy rainfall has been affecting northern, central and western Afghanistan since 10 May, causing flash floods, floods and mudslides, which have resulted in casualties and severe damage. The affected provinces are Baghlan, the worst affected, Badakhshan, Takhar, Ghor, and Herat.

UN and media report, as of 14 May, more than 330 fatalities, of which over 300 across the Baghlan province. In addition, media also report an uncertain number of displaced people, who will need temporary shelter. Around 3,000 destroyed houses were reported in the Baghlan province and approximately 300 across Takhar and Badakhshan provinces. At least 2,000 houses were damaged. Needs are for shelter, food, clean water and medical support.

name: OSMBD Mapathon with OpenStreetMap
shortDescription: The Geological formation of Chandpur was taken place in Pleistocene and Holocene Era. Geographical history of Chandpur was found in the East-Indian country-map of Perguitar. In the map, south to Bangladesh, Sagornooper, to the north Pragjyotish and the Eastern plain beside hills was known as ‘Kiratas.’ The then Red River (Brammhaputra of today) borne alluvial soil contributed the formation of ‘Kiratas’ and Comilla was under it. That is Chandpur was under ‘Kiratas.’ In the map of Tomas Water, a land named ‘Srikhetra’ was shown to the south of the combined course of both the Titas and Gomati (probably). It is guessed that Chandpur and the west part of Noakhali were under ‘Srikhetra.’ In the map of Jean de Brosse in 1560, ‘Tropo’ was shown by river banks. This ‘Tropo’ was actually Tripura or Comilla region. That is, Chandpur was a part of Tripura. In the map of Portuguese sailor Sanson de Abevil in 1652, Bander, a place was marked where there was a big river port. This port was actually Chandpur. In 1779, English surveyor Major James Rennel drew a map where not only Tripura, but also Chandpur and Comilla were rightly spotted.

name: Settlement Areas for Emergency basemaps - Maungdaw Township
shortDescription:
Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as MyOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. 

You can contribute by **mapping and updating settlement areas** based on satellite imagery. Your settlement areas will be complemented by roads, rivers and points of interests mapped through HOT tasks that will follow. 

Knowing where people live is essential to prepare for emergency assistance and to access those people and provide help when needed.

Your efforts contribute to map larger areas with the required level of accuracy and turn those into much needed basemaps for Myanmar and its people.

name: Eco Smart City Nigeria-Abeokuta & Environs
shortDescription:
The Eco-Smart Cities project aims to tackle the complex issues in urban centers within the region. It envisions a future where cities become lively and intelligent ecosystems. The project aims to address environmental degradation, limited resources, inadequate infrastructure, public health concerns, and economic inequalities through a comprehensive, open data and participatory mapping approach. This project will stimulate sustainable urban growth that benefits current and forthcoming generations. This will be achieved by collecting data, conducting analyses, and presenting information visually. This valuable data will aid city planners, national authorities, the private sector, and other stakeholders in making informed decisions and shaping urbanization strategies.
To address the challenges related to sustainability, a comprehensive strategy that considers the environmental, social, and economic dimensions is required. Data can play a crucial role in this process. Still, it is essential to ensure that all stakeholders - including governments, local authorities, and private sector partners - collaborate effectively to develop and implement sustainable policies. One of the initial steps in this journey is to accurately map the city's layout, including its structures, buildings, amenities, roads, waterways, and land use.

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is supporting local communities as well as those who have been temporarily displaced to Mizoram state in India following the conflict in Myanmar. These provinces where MSF works in Mizoram state are amongst the most impoverished of the districts in North-eastern India. Water, health care and sanitation needs are quite high, and infrastructure was already very weak for the host population before the influx of thousands displaced people into the villages.

MSF aims to provide free and quality medical and mental health care to the communities in the area, while responding to any medical-humanitarian emergency that may occur in Mizoram State. Activities include mobile medical clinics, mental health support, water and sanitation support and distributions of non-food items such as kitchen utensils & blankets.

name: Missing Maps: Roads & residential landuse in Sokoto, Nigeria (11)
shortDescription:
Since 2014, Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has been supporting aid in Sokoto, Nigeria. Particularly the Sokoto Noma Hospital, with a programme of activities for people affected by noma, including noma survivors and their families. Noma, a neglected and little-known non-contagious disease, mostly affects children under five living in poverty.

It starts as an inflammation of the gums, similar to a small mouth ulcer. In just two weeks the infection starts to destroy bone and tissue, potentially affecting the jaw, lips, cheeks, nose or eyes, leaving survivors with physical consequences including pain, breathing complications and difficulties eating. Noma has a strikingly high mortality rate, and those who do survive are left with life-changing facial disfigurements.

Four times a year, a team of international surgeons, anaesthesiologists and nurses travel to Sokoto Noma Hospital to operate on noma survivors. The hospital, run in collaboration with the Nigerian Ministry of Health, also focuses on community outreach, active case finding in the region, health promotion and mental health support. Better maps are needed in particular to support these community health activities.

To learn more about the noma disease you can check out [this page](https://noma.msf.org).

name: Roads for Emergency basemaps - Palaw Ts
shortDescription:
Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as MyOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. 

You can contribute by **mapping and updating roads** based on satellite imagery. Your settlement areas will be complemented by settlement areas, rivers and points of interests mapped through HOT tasks that will follow. 

Knowing where people live is essential to prepare for emergency assistance and to access those people and provide help when needed.

Your efforts contribute to map larger areas with the required level of accuracy and turn those into much needed basemaps for Myanmar and its people.

name: Missing Maps: Buildings in Mizoram State, India (19)
shortDescription:
Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is supporting local communities as well as those who have been temporarily displaced to Mizoram state in India following the conflict in Myanmar. These provinces where MSF works in Mizoram state are amongst the most impoverished of the districts in North-eastern India. Water, health care and sanitation needs are quite high, and infrastructure was already very weak for the host population before the influx of thousands displaced people into the villages.

MSF aims to provide free and quality medical and mental health care to the communities in the area, while responding to any medical-humanitarian emergency that may occur in Mizoram State. Activities include mobile medical clinics, mental health support, water and sanitation support and distributions of non-food items such as kitchen utensils & blankets. 

For MSF teams to carry out work in the area, mapping is required. The primary needs for mapping are the localisation of villages, buildings and roads. In this project you can help mapping buildings.

name: Mapping Eswatini for Resilient efforts_Piggs_Peak
shortDescription:
The mapping project for Eswatini aims to advance the Kingdoms mapped inventory by significantly enhancing OpenStreetMap data, addressing its current non-existence or outdated state. The project directly supports disaster response by ensuring precise geospatial data for crucial amenities, bolstering climate resilience and community well-being. The primary focus of the project is mapping essential geographic features like buildings, roads, amenities, and place names—critical elements for disaster preparedness and climate resilience in Eswatini. By meticulously mapping these areas, the NDMA can design effective disaster planning and response strategies, including early warning systems, evacuation routes, and resource allocation for relief efforts. 

At least 50,000 buildings, 600 kilometers of road, 25,000 amenities, and 1000 place names will be mapped to facilitate improved navigation, accessibility, and urban development planning.

Help updating the map of Camp 14 & 15 in the Kutupalong, Cox's Bazar refugee camp in Bangladesh.

name: Roads for Emergency basemaps - Kyunsu Township
shortDescription:
Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as MyOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. 

You can contribute by **mapping and updating roads** based on satellite imagery. Your settlement areas will be complemented by settlement areas, rivers and points of interests mapped through HOT tasks that will follow. 

Knowing where people live is essential to prepare for emergency assistance and to access those people and provide help when needed.

Your efforts contribute to map larger areas with the required level of accuracy and turn those into much needed basemaps for Myanmar and its people.

shortDescription: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) recently confirmed the development of El Niño conditions in the tropical Pacific after seven years. These conditions have led to disruptive weather patterns and climate changes globally. In Somalia, Drought and La Niña have significantly impacted the nation, exacerbating water shortages, crop failures, and livestock migration. In addition, Somalia has experienced three consecutive below-average rainy seasons, leading to severe drought conditions.

name: Mapping Landslide-Affected Areas in Gofa Zone, Southern Ethiopia:  Bulki
shortDescription:
The Open Mapping Hub Eastern and Southern Africa is collaborating with OpenStreetMap Ethiopia to provide open data for relief to landslide-affected communities in Gofa Zone, Southern Ethiopia.

On July 24, 2024, two catastrophic landslides struck the Kencho-Shacha locality in the Gofa zone, Southern Ethiopia, resulting in significant loss of life and property. These landslides, triggered by heavy rains, buried homes, and infrastructure, and displaced thousands. Accurate and up-to-date maps are crucial for guiding search and rescue operations, planning relief distribution, assessing damage, and facilitating long-term recovery and risk reduction efforts. This project aims to fill the existing data gap in the region, providing detailed maps that can be used by humanitarian organizations, local authorities, and community members to support their efforts.

The district is one of the ten districts of Saint Lucia and has a name derived from French origins with the English translation meaning Bay of Rays. Two rivers flow into the bay, these are the Grande Rivière de l'Anse la Raye and the Petite Rivière de l'Anse la Raye. The majority of community members reside in the village area. This positions over 500 households with the risk of coastal and flooding from the rivers. Join YEAC St Lucia volunteer mappers to assist with the Hazard, Vulnerability, and Capacity mapping of this community.
organisationName: Youth Emergency Action Committees St Lucia (YEAC)
author: Proann

name: Settlement Areas for Emergency basemaps - ANN Township (North)
shortDescription:
Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as MyOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. 

You can contribute by **mapping and updating settlement areas** based on satellite imagery. Your settlement areas will be complemented by roads, rivers and points of interests mapped through HOT tasks that will follow. 

Knowing where people live is essential to prepare for emergency assistance and to access those people and provide help when needed.

Your efforts contribute to map larger areas with the required level of accuracy and turn those into much needed basemaps for Myanmar and its people.
author: Chit San Ko

name: Eco Smart City Ghana - Koforidua
shortDescription: The Eco-Smart Cities project aims to transform urban centers into sustainable, intelligent ecosystems by addressing issues like environmental degradation, resource limitations, inadequate infrastructure, public health, and economic inequalities. The project uses open data and participatory mapping to collect and analyze information, which will guide city planners, national authorities, and other stakeholders in making informed decisions for sustainable urban growth. A comprehensive strategy considering environmental, social, and economic factors is crucial, and collaboration among governments, local authorities, and private sector partners is essential for developing and implementing effective policies. The initial step involves accurately mapping the city's layout and resources.

name: Mapeamento de edifícios no bairro São João (Alegrete, Rio Grande do Sul, Brasil)
shortDescription:
O bairro de São João, na cidade de Alegrete (estado do Rio Grande do Sul, Brasil), foi um dos locais atingidos pelo evento desastroso que acometeu o estado desde o final de abril de 2024, causando transtornos para seus residentes. 

Este é um projeto coordenado pelo IVIDES.org e que será desenvolvido pelos integrantes do HUB YouthMappers Rio de Janeiro e outros(as) mapeadores(as) brasileiros.

Este mapeamento tem o objetivo específico de mapear edificações, dados que são importantes para a prevenção e mitigação dos danos causados pelos desastres à população.

Esta atividade faz parte do evento maior, de comemoração dos 20 anos de OpenStreetMap, para saber mais, por gentileza, visite o portal https://ivides.org/20-anos-de-openstreetmap. 

Responsável: Dra. Raquel Dezidério Souto
Contato: ivides@ivides.org

name: REBUMAA (NIGERIA)
shortDescription:
The REBUMAA(Resilience Building through Multi-Stakeholder Engagement in Anticipatory Action for
Climate Induced Disaster) is a research project developed under the Climate Adaptation and Resilience (CLARE) initiative to support climate change, adaptation, resilience, and nature-based solution research in Benin, Nigeria, and Togo.

The overall objective of the project is to identify the barriers and limitations to organizational and structural capacities for the implementation of anticipatory action in disaster management with a view to developing best practices in multi-stakeholder governance of proactive and inclusive action in a harmonized context.

REBUMAA aims to achieve this by developing Early Action Protocols (EAPs) which have the potential to advance research on the forecast-based financing (FbF) approach and establish best practices for future implementation.

name: Roads for Emergency basemaps - Hlaingbwe Township
shortDescription:
Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as MyOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. 

You can contribute by **mapping and updating roads** based on satellite imagery. Your settlement areas will be complemented by settlement areas, rivers and points of interests mapped through HOT tasks that will follow. 

Knowing where people live is essential to prepare for emergency assistance and to access those people and provide help when needed.

Your efforts contribute to map larger areas with the required level of accuracy and turn those into much needed basemaps for Myanmar and its people.

name: Mapping Settlement Areas For Emergency Basemap - Thandaunggyi Township, Kayin State
shortDescription:
Thandaunggyi township, located in Kayin State, southeastern Myanmar, is a region characterized by its ethnic diversity and challenging geography. Accurate mapping of residential areas (settlements) is vital for planning and implementing humanitarian aid, development projects, and infrastructure improvements, especially in a region affected by ongoing conflicts and limited access to basic services.

Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as myOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. 

You can contribute by **mapping and updating settlement areas** based on satellite imagery. Your settlement areas will be complemented by roads, rivers and points of interests mapped through HOT tasks that will follow.

name: Settlement Areas for Emergency basemaps - Thaton Township
shortDescription:
English version: Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as MyOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. 

You can contribute by **mapping and updating settlement areas** based on satellite imagery. Your settlement areas will be complemented by roads, rivers and points of interests mapped through HOT tasks that will follow. 

Knowing where people live is essential to prepare for emergency assistance and to access those people and provide help when needed.

Your efforts contribute to map larger areas with the required level of accuracy and turn those into much needed basemaps for Myanmar and its people.

**> NOTE: This project is specifically designed for new OSMers to practice drawing settlement areas. Training for OSM mappers of myOSM from 2024 August 22 to 2024 September 22.**

**> Not for previous osmers.**

name: Nigeria Flooding: Maiduguri, Gwange 1
shortDescription:
Humanitarians are rushing to assist scores of newly displaced people in northeast Nigeria, after torrential rains caused a dam to collapse and flood the area. The dam collapse saw river water overrunning 50 per cent of Maiduguri and state authorities issued evacuation orders to residents in the affected areas, appealing for humanitarian support.

**More than 1,000,000 people have been displaced across northeast Nigeria, according to [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/flooding-northern-nigeria-borno-dam-collapse-60ed5b7bddfc4a5b65c0a0573d735d2b). MSF and the Nigerian Red Cross are both responding and in need of data.**

name: Roads for Emergency basemaps - Kalaw Township, Shan (South)
shortDescription:
Access to suitable basemaps for humanitarian and emergency operations in Myanmar is now more crucial than ever. No fit-for-purpose basemaps in adequate scale, showing essential features like roads, rivers, settlements, and critical infrastructure exit. As a result, civil society and aid organizations often rely on inadequate map like Google Maps, which lack sufficient detail esp. in rural areas, or have no suitable maps at all.

We as MyOSM, a dedicated group of OpenStreetMap supporters in Myanmar, are working to address this challenge with your assistance. 

You can contribute by **mapping and updating roads** based on satellite imagery. Your settlement areas will be complemented by settlement areas, rivers and points of interests mapped through HOT tasks that will follow. 

Knowing where people live is essential to prepare for emergency assistance and to access those people and provide help when needed.

Your efforts contribute to map larger areas with the required level of accuracy and turn those into much needed basemaps for Myanmar and its people.

name: Missing Maps: Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, Canada
shortDescription:
The Missing Maps project aims to map the most vulnerable places in the world (affected by humanitarian crises: disease epidemics, conflict, natural disasters, poverty, environmental crises). Building on HOT's disaster preparedness projects, the Missing Maps tasks facilitate pre-emptive mapping of priority countries to better facilitate disaster response, medical activities and resource allocation when crises occur.

Moose Jaw, located in south-central Saskatchewan, Canada, is a city of about 34,000, known for its strong industrial base in agriculture, potash mining, and transportation. It also hosts 15 Wing Moose Jaw, the home of the Snowbirds aerobatic team. Situated near the Moose Jaw River, the city receives precipitation influenced by surrounding water sources and runoff.

Flooding is a key concern, with the Water Security Agency identifying the city as high-risk, prompting mitigation measures. Other extreme weather events, such as severe snowstorms, tornadoes, and droughts, also impact Moose Jaw, affecting local infrastructure and agriculture. Although wildfires have not directly hit the city, smoke from regional fires and dry conditions pose air quality and grass fire risks.

Given these recurring natural threats, detailed mapping is essential to bolster disaster preparedness, facilitate emergency response, and enhance community resilience.

Mount Lewotobi Laki-Laki in East Flores Regency, East Nusa Tenggara (NTT), erupted early Monday (04/11). At least 10 people were killed, dozens more were injured, and several buildings were burned due to 'rain of material' from the eruption. 

The eruption disrupted activities at 66 educational institutions in Wulanggitang and Ile Bura sub-districts in East Flores district. Seventeen of the educational institutions suffered structural damage.

It also affected 458 teachers and 5,383 pupils in the two sub-districts.

Meanwhile, the National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) reported that 2,735 families, or 12,200 people, were affected by the Lewotobi Laki-laki eruption and sought shelter in safer places.

Deputy Home Minister Bima Arya Sugiarto also confirmed that the emergency response operation will take place until December 31, 2024.

name: Somalia, IDP Site Mapping, Kismayo
shortDescription:
**Ground Truth Solutions** plans to carry out door-to-door assessment visits covering all buildings in the most vulnerable areas of Kismayo to identify the poorest households and ensure no one is left behind. 

In order to do that, Ground Truth Solutions need the support of the OSM community to help map all the buildings in the selected areas, including host community and internally displaced persons (IDP) sites. Most host community areas are well-mapped, with few exceptions. However, this is not the case for IDP sites where most support is needed. The assignment includes adding new buildings using satellite imagery as well as making any necessary edits to already mapped buildings in case they do not match with the imagery.

name: Building Footprint Mapping - Taungyi Township, Shan State, Myanmar
shortDescription:
On September 8, Typhoon Yagi triggered severe flooding and landslides across Myanmar, impacting over 69 townships in nine states and regions: Bago, Kayah, Kayin, Magway, Mandalay, Mon, Nay Pyi Taw, and southern and eastern Shan. The flash floods resulted in numerous fatalities, while landslides buried many homes, particularly in Taungyi Township.

To support humanitarian aid organizations operating in Myanmar, mapping and improving settlement data (including building footprints) is crucial. This initiative is part of the State of Map (SoTM) Asia 2024, which features a remote mapathon organized by volunteers, AP Hub, and myOSM.

name: Lebanon Conflict: Bent Jbeil 2
shortDescription:
Recent conflict (2023-2024) has impacted the humanitarian situation in southern Lebanon. Despite a ceasefire in December 2024, humanitarian needs remain high. Much of the area has been damaged, disrupting essential services and impacting rebuilding. Early recovery actions require a baseline map of infrastructure to plan response as people attempt to return home. Data mapped here will be used to better understand damaged and functional infrastructure.

This project is part of a campaign to map buildings in conflict affected areas in Lebanon, starting with 7 districts in the south. Track live campaign progress [here](https://umap.openstreetmap.fr/en/map/lebanon-conflict-2024-tasking-manager-project-prog_1132719#10/33.3758/35.2359).

name: Mayotte (North East): Cyclone Chido Priority Areas
shortDescription:
On Saturday 14 December 2024, Tropical Cyclone Chido made landfall in Mayotte. It is considered the most violent and destructive cyclone to affect Mayotte since 1934. Up to 100,000 people (almost a third of the population of Mayotte) have been displaced by the storm and thousands more have been declared missing, including over 200 Red Cross volunteers. The French Interior Ministry has estimated 70% of the territory's population was severely affected. More info on [Wiki page EN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Chido) / [Wiki page FR](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Chido)

Please contribute to this project to support the response and recovery efforts in Mayotte. Although Mayotte is relatively well mapped on OSM, the data needs to be checked and there are some small data gaps that need filling. This project **uses very clear 20cm imagery from 2023**.

In this project we will map **residential areas**, **villages** and **hedges** supporting **UNSOS** to ensure peace in **Somalia**.

**You are required to carefully read all the instructions inside the project before starting to map**. Ask any mapping or validation question in the **Questions and comments section** below. 


**[UN Mappers](https://mappers.un.org/)** is a thriving community ranging from **UN personnel on the field** (GIS groups, UN offices, military and police) to **academia** (high schools and universities), from **local communities** and **NGOs** to **any remote volunteer** in the world. 


Don’t forget to follow our activities through our [social media](https://mappers.un.org/news/social-media) or [send us an e-mail](mailto:un.mappers@un.org) if you want to stay regularly updated on our mapping activities or to propose further engagements.

name: Mapping for Sudan :  Abu Ajura
shortDescription:
Since April 2023, the civil war in Sudan has led to deteriorating humanitarian conditions and damage to community infrastructure. A more precise building footprints dataset is needed to calculate more accurate estimates of damage to inform resource planning for a humanitarian response. Data is also needed to identify functional infrastructure and services to plan recovery efforts. Help by mapping buildings in urban centers in Sudan!  

Please see the [Contributor Guidelines](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18qEBLVYqUTpcy2pSHE3EUusDYLNSqGSoRHYiSadxt7Q/edit#heading=h.kxz2tjh007pe) (Google Document) for pointers on how to participate responsibly in areas of active conflict.

shortDescription: On Saturday 14 December, Cyclone Chido made landfall south of the city of Pemba in Mozambique as a Category 4 cyclone. name: DRP_Mapping_WVTL_Area Program_Fatululic
shortDescription:
This maping task has been developed to enhance disaster preparedness and response in the Fatululic Administrative Post, Covalima Municipality. It supports World Vision Timor-Leste’s disaster preparedness program, funded by the Australian Government through the Australia Humanitarian Partnership.
Fatululic is one of the most disaster-prone areas in Covalima, highly vulnerable to extreme weather events such as strong winds and landslides. With agriculture as the primary livelihood, the local community faces significant challenges in effectively responding to disasters. This mapping initiative aims to strengthen resilience and improve response mechanisms in the region.
